2027-01-01.title: The Holy Name of Jesus (Circumcision of our Lord) · New Year's Day
2027-01-01.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: God changes Abram's name and gives the covenant of circumcision
I have called you by name, you are mine
The name that is above every name
2027-01-01.alt: Also the First Friday of Nativity, which in this calendar is the last Friday of Nativity: the Divine Motherhood of Mary (Exodus 15:11–21; Acts 1:12–14; Romans 16:17–20, 25–27; Luke 1:39–45). New Year readings: Exodus 23:14–17; Isaiah 52:7–12; Ephesians 4:17–24; Matthew 6:25–34. Weekday readings: Hebrews 1:1–4; John 1:14–18.
2027-01-01.verse: She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
theo: On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised and “he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.” The Syro-Malabar Church begins the civil year with this feast of the Holy Name. In the first reading God changes Abram's name to Abraham and gives him the covenant sign; a new name means a new mission. Through Isaiah God says to his people: “I have called you by name, you are mine.” Names in the Bible are not labels; they reveal who someone is before God.

The name Jesus, Yeshua, means “the LORD saves”. The angel explains it to Joseph: “he will save his people from their sins.” And St Paul sings the hymn of Philippians: the Son emptied himself, took the form of a slave, became obedient to death on a cross, “Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend.” The way to the exalted Name passed through humility and the Cross.

Today is also the last Friday of the Nativity season, kept as the Divine Motherhood of Mary. The woman who gave the Child his human flesh is the Mother of God; she stands with the Apostles in prayer at the beginning of the Church (Acts 1:14). As the new year opens, the Church places on our lips the Name in which there is salvation, and under our eyes the Mother who keeps us close to her Son.
conn: Circumcision on the eighth day.
Genesis 17:12 commands it as the sign of the covenant. By submitting to the Law, the Son of God enters fully into the history of his people (Galatians 4:4).
Naming.
In Israel the father named the child. Joseph obeys the angel and names him Jesus, thus legally adopting him into David's line (Matthew 1:25).
The Name in Syriac prayer.
The East Syriac liturgy is full of the name Isho Mshiha, Jesus the Messiah. The Malayalam ഈശോ comes from this Syriac form.
Prayer of the Name.
The Jesus Prayer, “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner”, is loved in the Christian East as a way of praying without ceasing.
Divine Motherhood.
The Syro-Malabar calendar keeps the Divine Motherhood of Mary on the last Friday of the Nativity season. The Council of Ephesus (431) confessed Mary as Mother of God.
New Year.
The Church blesses time. Exodus 23:14–17 tells Israel to keep festivals for the Lord through the year: the calendar itself becomes worship.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Name of Jesus is invoked again and again. We receive the One whose Name means “the Lord saves”.
Begin the year by receiving Holy Communion with this prayer: Jesus, be my Saviour this year in every day.
outline: Ask: who gave you your name, and what does it mean?
God names Abraham and calls his people his own.
The meaning of the name Jesus.
Humility and the Cross lead to exaltation.
Joseph whispering the name Jesus over the Child.
live: Pray the Name
Pray the Jesus Prayer slowly ten times each morning this year.
Honour the Name (Philippians 2:10)
Bow your head at the name of Jesus, and never use it carelessly.
Bless the year
Gather your family tonight and consecrate the new year to Jesus under the protection of Mary.
Know your name
Find out the meaning of your baptismal name and the saint you are named after.
fathers: St Bernard of Clairvaux
The name of Jesus is honey in the mouth, music in the ear, joy in the heart.
St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)
His name is a treasure: whoever calls on it is rich, and whoever holds it is not poor.
magis: Prayer to Jesus by name; the Jesus Prayer.
Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church.
Mary in the mystery of Christ and the Church.
saints: 2 Jan: First Saturday of Nativity. 3 Jan: Second Sunday of Nativity; St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan: Denha.
2027-01-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, your Name means “the Lord saves”. At the beginning of this new year we bow before your holy Name, which is above every name. Write your Name on our hearts, save us from our sins, and keep us all through this year under the mantle of your Mother, the Mother of God. To you be glory with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and for ever. Amen.

2027-01-03.title: First Sunday of Denha (Sunday before Denha)
2027-01-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I have come down to deliver them
Cyrus, the Lord's anointed, called by name
Salvation through faith in Christ Jesus
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me
2027-01-03.alt: The calendar counts this Sunday before the feast as the First Sunday of Denha. 3 January is also the feast of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara (Genesis 12:1–4; Isaiah 44:1–4; 1 Peter 4:12–19; Matthew 5:1–12); where it is kept, follow the local direction. The feast of Denha is on Wednesday 6 January: remind the faithful.
2027-01-03.verse: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor.
theo: Three days before the feast of Denha the Church already looks toward the Jordan, where the Spirit will come down upon Jesus. Today's readings speak of God the liberator and of those he sends. At the burning bush God tells Moses: “I have observed the misery of my people who are in Egypt; I have heard their cry on account of their taskmasters. Indeed, I know their sufferings, and I have come down to deliver them.” Then he sends a shepherd who protests, “Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh”, and who receives the only answer that matters: “I will be with you.”

Isaiah goes further. God calls a pagan king, Cyrus of Persia, his anointed, takes him by the right hand and says: “I call you by your name, I surname you, though you do not know me.” If God can use a foreign king to bring his people home from exile, nothing lies outside his reach. Yet Moses and Cyrus are only signs. In the synagogue of Nazareth Jesus unrolls the scroll of Isaiah and reads: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor.” Then he sits down and, with every eye fixed on him, says: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” The true Anointed, the Mshiha, has come. The freedom he brings is freedom from sin and death, and it begins with the poor.

St Paul shows how this freedom reaches every generation. He reminds Timothy of the faith he received at home: “from childhood you have known the sacred writings that are able to instruct you for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.” Faith passes from parent to child and from teacher to pupil, and it holds firm through persecution. St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, whose feast falls today, lived this: a son of Kainakary who, like Moses, heard the cry of his people, and who asked that a school stand beside every church, so that every child might come to know the Scriptures and the way of salvation.
conn: The Sunday before Denha.

This year the calendar counts the Sunday that falls before the feast of 6 January as the First Sunday of Denha. Its readings already sound the theme of the season: God revealing the one he has anointed and sent.
The burning bush.

The bush burned but was not consumed (Exodus 3:2). Eastern Fathers, among them St Gregory of Nyssa, saw in it an image of the Virgin Mary, who carried the divine fire in her womb and was not consumed.
Cyrus, the anointed.
Cyrus II of Persia took Babylon in 539 BC and allowed the exiles to return and rebuild the Temple (Ezra 1:1–4). He is the only non-Israelite in the Old Testament called the Lord's anointed.
The reading at Nazareth.
Jesus reads Isaiah 61:1–2, with a phrase from Isaiah 58:6. He stops before the words about the day of vengeance: he comes first to proclaim the year of the Lord's favour.
Timothy's home.
St Paul praises the sincere faith that lived first in Timothy's grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice (2 Timothy 1:5). The Scriptures he knew from childhood were learned at home.
St Chavara.
St Kuriakose Elias Chavara (1805–1871), co-founder of the CMI and founder of the CMC congregations, pioneered schools beside churches and printed Malayalam books at Mannanam. Canonised in 2014.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is our synagogue of Nazareth: the Word is proclaimed, and the Church believes that in Christ it is fulfilled today. What is proclaimed from the bema is given at the altar.
At the altar the Anointed One, on whom the Spirit rests, comes down to his people as God came down at the burning bush: not to consume us but to set us free.
outline: Ask: who taught you the faith when you were a child?
Point 1 · God hears and comes down
Point 2 · Who am I? I will be with you
Cyrus a sign; Jesus the Anointed.
Faith handed on, as St Chavara taught.
“Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
live: Hear the cry (Exodus 3:7)
Find out one real need in your parish or neighbourhood this week and do something about it.
Answer like Moses (Exodus 3:12)
When you feel unworthy of a task God gives you, pray: Lord, you will be with me.
Hand on the Scriptures (2 Timothy 3:15)
Read a Gospel passage aloud with your children or grandchildren before Denha.
Imitate St Chavara
Support a poor child's education this year.
fathers: Origen (in substance)
Blessed was that synagogue in which the eyes of all were fixed on Jesus. May our assemblies also look on him; when the eyes of the heart are fixed on the Word, his light shines on our faces.
St Gregory of Nyssa (in substance)
The light that shone from a thorn bush without burning it shows the mystery of the Virgin: from her the divine light shone into our life, and her virginity was not consumed.
magis: God reveals his name at the burning bush.
Jesus, the Christ, the Anointed One.
The Spirit of the Lord upon the Messiah (Luke 4:18).
Parents, the first educators in the faith.
saints: 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan: Denha (Baptism of the Lord). 8 Jan: St John the Baptist (First Friday of Denha).
2027-01-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, Anointed of the Father, the Spirit of the Lord is upon you, and you came to bring good news to the poor and release to the captives. You hear our cry as God heard Israel at the burning bush. Send us, as you sent Moses, with the promise that you will be with us; keep us in the faith we learned from childhood; and through the prayers of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara make our homes and schools places where your word is loved. Glory to you with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-06.title: Denha · The Epiphany and Baptism of our Lord
2027-01-06.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: A star shall come out of Jacob
The spirit of the Lord shall rest on him
The water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit
This is my Son, the Beloved
2027-01-06.alt: Important feast and day of obligation. The Third Qudasha (anaphora) is used in the Holy Qurbana. Beginning of the Season of Denha.
2027-01-06.verse: And a voice from heaven said, “This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.”
theo: Denha is a Syriac word meaning dawn, rising, manifestation. The Eastern Churches celebrate on this day not first the Magi but the Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan, because there the whole mystery of God shone out: the Son in the water, the Spirit descending like a dove, the Father's voice from heaven: “This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.” At the Jordan the Holy Trinity is revealed, and the public ministry of Jesus begins. The Sun of Justice rises over the world.

The readings show a dawn long promised. The seer Balaam, a stranger to Israel, looks out from the hills of Moab and sees far ahead: “I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near”, and he announces that “a star shall come out of Jacob”. Isaiah sees a shoot from the stump of Jesse and promises: “The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might”. At the Jordan both promises meet. The star has risen, and the Spirit comes down and rests on Jesus, as Matthew says: “he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him.”

John protests: “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?” Jesus had no sin. Yet he answers that “it is proper for us in this way to fulfill all righteousness”: he goes down into the water to stand with sinners and to sanctify the waters for us. St Paul tells Titus what this means for us: God “saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit. This Spirit he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior”. Our ancestors' customs, the lamps on plantain stems with the cry El Paiya, God is light, and the night bath recalling the Jordan, were ways of saying: our Baptism has made us children of light. Denha calls each of us to remember our Baptism and to live as beloved sons and daughters.
conn: Denha.
Syriac for dawn or rising. The feast is called Denha (Epiphany) in the East Syriac tradition, and in Kerala popularly Pindikuthi in the north and Rakkuli in the south.
Pindikuthi.
Lamps were fixed on a plantain stem (pindi) and the family processed around it crying “El Paiya”, a Syriac-Malayalam cry meaning God is light. Christ is the light of the world.
Rakkuli.
On the eve, families bathed in rivers or ponds at night (rakkuli, “night bath”), recalling the Jordan. It was a religious act of remembering Baptism, not a magical rite.
A star out of Jacob.

Balaam, a seer from outside Israel, foretells a star and a sceptre (Numbers 24:17). Many Fathers linked this star with the star of the Magi; the East Syriac tradition keeps the whole manifestation of Christ in this one feast.
To fulfil all righteousness.

Only Matthew records John's protest and Jesus' reply (Matthew 3:14–15). Jesus takes his place among sinners, as the Servant who will bear their sins, and so begins the obedience that leads to the Cross.
Blessing of water.
In many Eastern Churches water is solemnly blessed at Denha, because Christ sanctified the waters by his baptism (CCC 1224).
The Fridays of Denha.

On the Fridays of this season the Church remembers the great witnesses of Christ: John the Baptist, Peter and Paul, the Evangelists, Stephen, the Greek and Syrian Fathers, and finally all the faithful departed.
altar: The Third Qudasha is used today, with its rich prayers on the Holy Trinity. At the Jordan the Trinity was revealed; at the altar the Trinity gives us the Body and Blood of the Son by the Spirit.
In Baptism we went down into the water with Christ; in the Holy Qurbana we are fed as beloved children.
outline: Ask: do you know the date of your Baptism?
Point 2 · The Spirit rests on him
The Spirit of wisdom alights on Jesus.
Son, Spirit and the Father's voice.
The water of rebirth and the Spirit poured out on us.
A plantain stem with small lamps, and a family crying “El Paiya”.
live: Remember your Baptism
Find out your baptismal date and keep it like a birthday.
Bless with holy water
Keep holy water at home and bless yourself and your children each night.
Live the new birth (Titus 3:1–2)
This week speak evil of no one and show courtesy to everyone, as Paul asks of the baptised.
Keep the custom
Teach children the meaning of Pindikuthi and Rakkuli.
fathers: St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)
Fire and Spirit are in the river in which you were baptised: the Jordan received the One who is fire, and the waters were made holy.
St Gregory Nazianzen (in substance)
Christ is baptised: let us go down with him, so that we may also rise with him.
magis: Baptism makes us children of God and members of the Church.
The Eastern liturgy as a feast of light and theophany.
saints: 8 Jan: First Friday of Denha, St John the Baptist. 10 Jan: Second Sunday of Denha.
2027-01-06.prayer: O Christ, Sun of Justice, today you rose upon the world at the Jordan. The Father bore witness to you, and the Spirit of wisdom came down and rested on you. Sanctify us who were washed in the water of rebirth; pour out your Spirit richly upon us; and let us live as beloved children of light. To you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be praise and glory, now and always and for ever. Amen.

2027-01-10.title: Second Sunday of Denha
2027-01-10.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The ark of the covenant went before them
Israel is saved by the Lord with everlasting salvation
Jesus is worthy of more glory than Moses
Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ
2027-01-10.verse: And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
theo: Denha celebrates the manifestation of the Lord, and today's Gospel puts its heart into one sentence: “And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory.” The Greek verb means that the Word pitched his tent among us. Israel already knew a God who travels with his people. In the Book of Numbers the tribes leave Sinai “with the ark of the covenant of the LORD going before them three days' journey, to seek out a resting place for them”, and the cloud of the Lord is over them by day. Whenever the ark set out, Moses prayed: “Arise, O LORD, let your enemies be scattered.” God did not stay on the mountain; he went ahead of his people on the road.

Isaiah confesses the same mystery from the other side: “Truly, you are a God who hides himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.” The Creator whose hands stretched out the heavens is beyond our sight, and yet he saves: “Israel is saved by the LORD with everlasting salvation.” John answers this longing of every human heart: “No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, who has made him known.” The hidden God has shown his face in Jesus. That is Denha: the God who hides himself becomes visible in a child of Nazareth, in a man baptised in the Jordan, in the Lord who walks the road with us.

The Letter to the Hebrews compares Moses and Jesus. Moses was faithful in God's house as a servant; “Christ, however, was faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.” John says the same: “The law indeed was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.” The law was a gift; Christ is the Giver himself. “From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.” In the Holy Qurbana that fullness is offered to us again: the Word who pitched his tent among us dwells on our altar and in our hearts, and we become his house, his tent among the nations.
conn: Pitched his tent.
The Greek word in John 1:14 (eskēnōsen) recalls the tent of meeting in the wilderness, where the glory of the Lord dwelt in the midst of Israel. Jesus is God's dwelling with his people.
The ark.
The ark of the covenant held the tablets of the law. It went before Israel as the sign of God's presence. The Fathers saw in it a figure of Christ, and also of Mary, who carried the Word in her womb.
Arise, O Lord.
Moses' prayer when the ark set out (Numbers 10:35) is echoed at the start of Psalm 68 and is still said in synagogues when the Torah scroll is taken out for reading.
Cyrus.
Isaiah 45 speaks of Cyrus, the Persian king whom God raised up to free the exiles (45:1, 13). God guides history even through those who do not know him.
Apostle and high priest.
Hebrews 3:1 is the only place in the New Testament where Jesus himself is called an apostle: the one sent by the Father.
The Gospel honoured.
In the Holy Qurbana the Gospel is proclaimed with lights and incense, because in it the Word who dwelt among us speaks to his people today.
altar: The Word who became flesh and lived among us gives himself on the altar under the signs of bread and wine. The tent of meeting has become the Holy Qurbana.
John says that from his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. At Communion we receive that fullness: Christ himself.
outline: Ask: if you could see God for one minute, what would you hope to see?
Point 1 · The ark goes before us
Point 2 · A God who hides himself
Christ is Son over God's house, and we are his house.
The fullness we receive in Christ.
A tent pitched in the middle of the camp, with a lamp burning inside.
“Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.”
live: Read the Prologue
Read John 1:1–18 slowly once this week and stop at the verse that touches you.
Let the Lord go first (Numbers 10:35)
Before you leave home each morning, pray as Moses did: Arise, O Lord, go before me today.
Seek the hidden God
Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament, where the Lord hides himself in order to stay near us.
Count grace upon grace (John 1:16)
Each night write down one grace you received that day.
fathers: St Athanasius (in substance)
The Word became man so that we might share in the life of God; he took what is ours in order to give us what is his.
St Augustine (in substance)
Christ as man is the way, Christ as God is the homeland. Walk by the man, and you will come to God.
magis: In his Son the Father has said everything; there will be no other word.
Christ's whole life reveals the Father.
God speaks to us as friends and lives among us.
saints: 14 Jan: St Devasahayam. 15 Jan: Second Friday of Denha, Sts Peter and Paul.
2027-01-10.prayer: O Lord our God, you went before your people in the ark and in the cloud, and in the fullness of time your eternal Word became flesh and pitched his tent among us. Grant that we who have received from his fullness grace upon grace may hold firm our hope, become your living house, and walk with him until we see your glory face to face. To you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, be glory, now and always and for ever. Amen.

2027-01-17.title: Third Sunday of Denha
2027-01-17.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Moses bears the burden of his people
Turn to me and be saved; I will carry and will save
Let us enter the Lord's rest through faith
The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world
2027-01-17.alt: Season of Denha. The Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu) begins tomorrow, Monday 18 January: remind the faithful. The Church Unity Octave also begins tomorrow.
2027-01-17.verse: even to your old age I am he, even when you turn gray I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save.
theo: This Sunday asks a simple question: who carries whom? Moses, worn out by a complaining people, cries to God: “I am not able to carry all this people alone, for they are too heavy for me.” He even asks God whether he must “carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a sucking child”. God does not scold him. He takes some of the spirit that is on Moses and gives it to seventy elders, so that “they shall bear the burden of the people along with you so that you will not bear it all by yourself.”

Isaiah answers the question with a picture from Babylon. On feast days the statues of the gods were carried through the streets; now, says the prophet, “Bel bows down, Nebo stoops”, loaded on weary animals, idols that must be carried and cannot save. The God of Israel is the opposite: his people have been “borne by me from your birth, carried from the womb”, and he promises: “even when you turn gray I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save.” So he can call the whole world: “Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth!”

In the Gospel John the Baptist sees Jesus coming and cries: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” The Lamb lifts and carries away the weight that no Moses could carry: the sin of the world. John testifies that the Spirit came down and remained on him, and that “this is the Son of God.” Hebrews adds the goal of the journey: “a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God”, and the door is open “today”. Tomorrow we begin the Three Days' Fast. We fast not to carry ourselves by our own strength, but to hand our burden to the Lamb who carries it, and to enter his rest.
conn: Moses' honest prayer.

Moses tells God exactly how tired he is (Numbers 11:11–15). Scripture keeps such prayers so that we may pray our exhaustion too. God answers by sharing the Spirit with seventy elders (11:16–17): a first picture of shared ministry among God's people.
Bel and Nebo.

Bel (Marduk) and Nebo were the chief gods of Babylon; their statues were carried in procession at the New Year feast. Isaiah sees them carried off on pack animals, while the LORD carries his people (Isaiah 46:1–4).
The Lamb of God.

John's title gathers the Passover lamb whose blood saved Israel (Exodus 12), the lamb God provides for Abraham (Genesis 22:8) and the Servant led like a lamb to the slaughter (Isaiah 53:7). The Catechism sees in it Christ's whole mission of redemption (CCC 608).
God's rest.

Hebrews reads Psalm 95: the desert generation did not enter the land, and Joshua did not give the final rest (Hebrews 4:8). The rest that remains is God's own, begun in Christ and completed in heaven (CCC 1720).
Moonnu Nombu.

The Three Days' Fast of the Ninevites is kept in the East Syriac tradition from the sixth century, when a plague in Persia ended after the people fasted and prayed. It falls on the Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of the third week before the Great Fast (in 2027, 18–20 January).
Kuravilangad.
In Kerala, Kuravilangad Marth Mariam church is especially famous for its Moonnu Nombu pilgrimage and the ship procession (kappal pradakshinam) recalling Jonah's voyage.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world is offered and given to us. He who carried our sins now carries us.
Each Sunday Qurbana is a foretaste of the sabbath rest that remains for the people of God.
outline: Ask: what is the heaviest thing you have ever had to carry, in your arms or in your heart?
Moses cannot carry the people alone; God shares the Spirit.
Point 2 · Idols are carried; God carries
Bel and Nebo on weary animals; the LORD carries his people.
John points to the One who carries the sin of the world.
Hebrews: the rest remains; do not harden your hearts.
A father carrying a sleeping child home from a late Qurbana.
live: Prepare for the fast
Plan how you will keep Moonnu Nombu: food, prayer, confession.
Share a burden (Numbers 11:17)
Offer to carry part of someone's load this week: a chore, a visit, a hospital night.
Name your idol
Ask what you are carrying around that cannot save you, and put it down.
Unity Octave
Pray each day for the unity of all Christians.
fathers: St Cyril of Alexandria (in substance)
One Lamb died for all, to gather the whole flock of the earth back to God the Father; the sin of the world is taken away by the One who bore it.
St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)
The Ninevites fasted for three days and the threatened city was saved; let us also turn, and the gate of mercy will open.
magis: Jesus, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
God does not abandon his creatures; he upholds and sustains them.
The beatitude to which God calls us: entering into God's rest.
Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches, can. 882
Days of fasting and penance in the Eastern Churches.
saints: 18–20 Jan: Moonnu Nombu. 18–25 Jan: Church Unity Octave. 20 Jan: St Sebastian. 22 Jan: Third Friday of Denha, the Evangelists.
2027-01-17.prayer: Lord our God, you carried your people from the womb and promised to carry them to old age. When our burdens are too heavy for us, give us your Spirit and companions to share them. Take away our sins through your Lamb, and as we begin the fast of the Ninevites, let us not harden our hearts today, but enter the rest you have prepared. Glory to you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-24.title: Fourth Sunday of Denha
2027-01-24.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The LORD's power is not limited
I will put salvation in Zion, for Israel my glory
Christ, the eternal priest, is able to save
Jesus reveals his glory at Cana
2027-01-24.alt: Season of Denha. Church Unity Octave concludes tomorrow, the Conversion of St Paul.
2027-01-24.verse: Jesus did this, the first of his signs, in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.
theo: Denha is the season of Christ's manifestation, and the Church has long kept three manifestations together: the star that led the Magi, the voice and the dove at the Jordan, and the wine at Cana. Today the third is read. But the first reading prepares the ground. In the wilderness Moses cannot see how so many people will be fed, and God answers him: “Is the LORD's power limited? Now you shall see whether my word will come true for you or not.” God shares the spirit that was on Moses with seventy elders, and even Eldad and Medad, who stayed in the camp, prophesy. When Joshua wants them stopped, Moses says: “Would that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!” Then come the quails, more than anyone can gather; but the people seize them with greed, and the place is called the graves of craving. God's gifts can be received with gratitude or grabbed with craving.

Isaiah mocks the idols that must be lifted onto shoulders and carried, that stand where they are put and cannot answer anyone in trouble. The living God is the opposite: he carries his people. “I am God, and there is no one like me”, he says, and he promises: “I will put salvation in Zion, for Israel my glory.” At Cana that glory appears in the most ordinary place, a village wedding where the wine has run out. The mother of Jesus notices first and says simply, “They have no wine.” Jesus answers, “Woman, what concern is that to you and to me? My hour has not yet come.” She does not argue; she turns to the servants: “Do whatever he tells you.” Six stone jars stand there, meant for the Jewish rites of purification. They are filled to the brim with water, and the water becomes wine, so good that the steward tells the bridegroom, “you have kept the good wine until now.” John says Jesus “revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.”

Hebrews explains who is at work here. The priests of the old covenant were many, because death kept ending their service; but Christ “holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever”, and “he always lives to make intercession for them.” He offered sacrifice “once for all when he offered himself.” The jars of purification are filled with something new: not a rite repeated again and again, but the gift of the Bridegroom himself. Just before Cana, Philip tells the doubting Nathanael, “Come and see”, and Jesus promises him, “You will see greater things than these.” The greater thing is the hour that had not yet come: the Cross, where the true wine of the new covenant is poured out, and which every Holy Qurbana makes present for us.
conn: Three manifestations.
Eastern and Western tradition alike join the Magi, the Baptism and Cana as the threefold manifestation of Christ celebrated in this season.
Kibroth-hattaavah.
The name means “graves of craving” (Numbers 11:34): the people received God's gift with greed instead of gratitude.
Eldad and Medad.
The spirit falls even on those outside the tent; Moses' wish is fulfilled at Pentecost, when the Spirit is poured out on all (Acts 2:17).
Idols carried, God who carries.
Isaiah 46 contrasts gods that must be carried on shoulders with the LORD who carries Israel from birth to old age (Isaiah 46:3–4).
“Woman”.
Not a cold word but a solemn title; Jesus uses it again from the Cross (John 19:26). Cana and Calvary are linked by the “hour”.
Six stone jars.
Each held twenty or thirty gallons: an overflowing abundance, a sign that the messianic wedding feast has begun (Isaiah 25:6; Amos 9:13).
altar: At Cana water became wine; at the altar the wine becomes the Blood of Christ, the good wine kept until now.
Christ, who always lives to intercede for us, offers himself in every Holy Qurbana, and his mother still tells us: Do whatever he tells you.
outline: Ask: what has run out in your home or your heart?
Point 1 · Is the LORD's power limited?
Moses' doubt, the Spirit shared, the graves of craving.
Idols carried on shoulders; the LORD carries us.
Point 3 · Do whatever he tells you
Mary notices, Jesus acts, the jars overflow.
The good wine kept until now.
Six stone jars filled to the brim.
live: Tell Jesus what has run out
Name one need of your family in prayer today, as Mary did: they have no wine.
Do whatever he tells you
Obey one clear word of the Gospel this week without delay.
Receive, do not crave
Before each meal this week, give thanks slowly instead of rushing to eat.
Pray for married couples
Pray for one couple whose love has run dry.
fathers: St Augustine (in substance)
He who made wine at Cana makes it every year in the vines from the rain; we do not marvel because it happens daily. At Cana he did quickly what he always does.
St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)
The guests praised the wine; let us praise the Giver, who now pours for us his own Blood in the cup of salvation.
magis: Jesus' presence at Cana confirms the goodness of marriage and makes it an efficacious sign of his presence.
Mary's prayer at Cana: the Mother of God's confident request.
The sign of water changed into wine at Cana announces the hour of Jesus' glorification and the Eucharist.
Christ the one high priest who always lives to make intercession; the one priesthood of Christ.
Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches, can. 776
Marriage as a covenant raised by Christ to the dignity of a sacrament.
saints: 25 Jan: Conversion of St Paul; Unity Octave ends. 26 Jan: Republic Day; Sts Timothy and Titus. 28 Jan: St Thomas Aquinas. 29 Jan: Fourth Friday of Denha, St Stephen. 31 Jan: Fifth Sunday of Denha; St John Bosco.
2027-01-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, at Cana you revealed your glory and filled the empty jars with the good wine. Free us from craving and teach us to receive your gifts with thanks. Through the prayers of your mother, who tells us to do whatever you say, fill our homes with your joy, and as our eternal priest who always intercedes for us, bring us to the wedding feast of heaven. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-31.title: Fifth Sunday of Denha
2027-01-31.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you and leads you
The light has come into the world
2027-01-31.alt: Season of Denha. St John Bosco: Philippians 4:4–9; Matthew 18:1–5.
2027-01-31.verse: “For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.
theo: As Israel stands at the edge of the promised land, Moses warns them not to seek the future through soothsayers and diviners, as the nations do: “You must remain completely loyal to the LORD your God.” Instead God makes a promise: “The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.” At Horeb the people had been terrified by the fire and the voice, and God answered their fear with tenderness: “I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.” Israel waited for that prophet for centuries. In Isaiah the same God speaks to his exiles in Babylon: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your own good, who leads you in the way you should go. O that you had paid attention to my commandments! Then your prosperity would have been like a river.” God is not a distant force to be manipulated by horoscopes and lucky times; he is a teacher who wants to lead us.

In the Gospel the Prophet like Moses speaks at night to Nicodemus. He recalls a strange scene from the wilderness: when the people were dying from serpent bites, Moses lifted up a bronze serpent on a pole, and whoever looked at it lived. “And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.” The Cross is the pole, and the One lifted up is the Son. Then comes the verse that sums up the whole Gospel: “For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.” God did not send his Son “to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him.” Judgment is not God's revenge; it is our choice: “the light has come into the world, and people loved darkness rather than light.”

Hebrews encourages Christians who have grown tired: “God is not unjust; he will not overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints.” Do not become sluggish; imitate “those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.” Abraham waited long, and “having patiently endured, obtained the promise.” Denha reveals Christ as the Prophet who speaks God's words, the Son lifted up for our healing, and the Light that shows our deeds as they are. “But those who do what is true come to the light.” Today the Church also remembers St John Bosco, who brought countless poor boys of Turin out of the streets and into the light of Christ, with patience, joy and a deep love for the Eucharist and Our Lady.
conn: A prophet like Moses.
The people asked John the Baptist, “Are you the prophet?” (John 1:21); Peter applied Deuteronomy 18 to Jesus (Acts 3:22).
Soothsayers and diviners.
Deuteronomy 18 forbids seeking the future through divination; the Church likewise rejects horoscopes, astrology and recourse to mediums (CCC 2115–2116).
The bronze serpent.
Numbers 21:8–9. Wisdom 16:6–7 calls it a symbol of deliverance: it was not the image that saved but God, the Saviour of all.
Lifted up.
In John the word means both crucifixion and exaltation (John 8:28; 12:32): the Cross is Christ's throne of glory.
Nicodemus by night.
He came to Jesus in the dark (John 3:2) and later came to the light, bringing myrrh and aloes for Jesus' burial (John 19:39).
God swore by himself.
The oath to Abraham (Genesis 22:16–17) shows that God's promise cannot fail; Hebrews calls our hope an anchor of the soul (Hebrews 6:19).
altar: The Son lifted up on the Cross is lifted up again in the hands of the priest before Communion, so that all who look on him with faith may have life.
At every Holy Qurbana the Prophet like Moses speaks God's word to us, and the Light of the world gives himself as food.
outline: Ask: where do people around you look to know the future?
Point 2 · The God who teaches and leads
Point 3 · Lifted up for our healing
The serpent, the Cross, and God's love for the world.
Patience, diligence, and deeds done in God.
A bronze serpent on a pole, and a Cross above it.
“For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.”
live: Renounce superstition
Remove any horoscope, lucky charm or reliance on auspicious times from your life, and trust God's providence.
Look at the Cross (John 3:14)
Spend five minutes each day this week looking at a crucifix in silence.
Come to the light (John 3:21)
Bring one hidden fault to the sacrament of Reconciliation.
Honour Don Bosco
Spend time with a young person, encouraging them in faith or study.
fathers: St Augustine (in substance)
Those bitten in the wilderness looked at the serpent and lived; so those wounded by sin look in faith on the death of Christ and are healed.
St John Chrysostom (in substance)
He did not give a servant, nor an angel, but his only Son: the greatness of the gift shows the greatness of the love.
magis: The Word became flesh so that we might know God's love: God so loved the world.
Christ came not to condemn but to save; whoever rejects the grace offered judges himself.
Divination, horoscopes and astrology contradict the honour and trust we owe to God alone.
Hope, the anchor of the soul, sustained by God's promise.
Christ, the Word made flesh, perfects and completes revelation.
saints: 2 Feb: Presentation of the Lord (Mayaltho). 3 Feb: St Blaise. Fifth week of Denha continues.
2027-01-31.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Prophet like Moses and only Son of the Father, you were lifted up on the Cross so that all who believe in you may have eternal life. Free us from every superstition and every darkness, teach us and lead us in the way we should go, give us patience to inherit your promises, and through the prayers of St John Bosco help us bring the young into your light. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-02.title: First Saturday of Nativity
2027-01-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: We have received the Spirit that is from God
Be dressed for action and have your lamps lit
2027-01-02.verse: You also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an unexpected hour.
theo: The Nativity season closes with a lamp in the hand. Jesus tells his disciples: “Be dressed for action and have your lamps lit; be like those who are waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet”. The servant's task is simple: stay awake, keep the lamp burning, open the door the moment the master knocks. Then comes a surprise that only the Child of Bethlehem can explain: “he will fasten his belt and have them sit down to eat, and he will come and serve them.” The Lord who came as a servant in the manger will come again as a servant at the table of his kingdom.

How do we stay awake? St Paul answers with the gift of the Spirit. As only a person's own spirit knows what is within, so “no one comprehends what is truly God's except the Spirit of God.” And “we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that is from God, so that we may understand the gifts bestowed on us by God.” The unspiritual person finds God's gifts foolish; the spiritual person discerns. Vigilance is not anxious clock-watching. It is a heart taught by the Spirit to recognise the Lord when he knocks: in prayer, in the poor at the gate, in the events of a new year. “You also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an unexpected hour.”
outline: Ask: what helps you to stay awake when you are waiting for someone you love?
Point 1 · The Spirit who knows God
Only the Spirit reveals what is God's.
The spiritual person sees with God's eyes.
Ready for the Master who comes to serve.
live: Ask for discernment (1 Corinthians 2:12)
Before each decision this week, pause and pray: Holy Spirit, show me what is from God.
Keep the lamp lit (Luke 12:35)
Choose a fixed moment each night this year for a short examination of conscience.
2027-01-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came among us as one who serves, and you will come again at an hour we do not know. Pour your Spirit into my heart, that I may discern what is from God, keep my lamp burning, and open the door to you whenever you knock. Amen.
altar: At every Holy Qurbana the Master who will come in glory already fastens his belt and serves us at his table (Luke 12:37). Each Qurbana prepares us for his coming.

2027-01-04.title: First Monday of Denha
2027-01-04.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set readings for this day not found; Second Set given, verify locally)
readings: Whatever is born of God conquers the world
The Son does what he sees the Father doing
2027-01-04.verse: for whatever is born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.
theo: As Denha draws near, the Church asks who the Child is. Jesus answers in the Gospel: “the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.” This is not weakness but perfect unity. The Son gives life as the Father gives life, and judges as the Father has entrusted to him, “so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.” The Child of Bethlehem is worthy of the same worship as the Father.

St John draws out what this means for believers: “Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God.” Faith is a new birth. And this new birth is strong: “whatever is born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.” The world with its fears, temptations and pressures does not have the last word over a child of God.
outline: Ask: what in the world around you seems stronger than your faith?
Point 2 · The Son and the Father
One in work, one in honour.
The victory that overcomes the world.
“This is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.”
live: Honour the Son (John 5:23)
Make a slow, reverent Sign of the Cross each time you pray today.
Overcome by faith (1 John 5:4)
Face one fear today with an act of faith: Jesus, I trust in you.
2027-01-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal Son of the Father, you do the works of the Father and give life to whom you will. I believe that you are the Christ; let this faith be my victory over every fear and temptation. Glory to you with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we give glory to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit together. The Son receives the same honour as the Father.

2027-01-05.title: First Tuesday of Denha · Eve of Denha
2027-01-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Strive to enter through the narrow door
2027-01-05.alt: Season of Denha. Tonight many families keep the Denha customs: lamps on plantain stems (pindikuthi) and the night bath recalling the Jordan (rakkuli).
2027-01-05.verse: Strive to enter through the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
theo: On the eve of Denha St Paul gives Titus a short rule for the baptised. Just before today's passage he has spoken of “the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit”; now he adds: “The saying is sure. I desire that you insist on these things, so that those who have come to believe in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works”. Baptism is not a certificate to be filed away; it is a new life to be lived in deeds. Paul also warns against the opposite: “stupid controversies, genealogies, dissensions, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and worthless.” A Christian community can waste its strength in endless arguments while the poor wait at the door.

In the Gospel someone asks Jesus: “Lord, will only a few be saved?” Jesus does not feed curiosity; he speaks to the heart: “Strive to enter through the narrow door”. To have eaten and drunk in his presence is not enough; what counts is a life he can recognise as his own. Yet the door is not narrow because God is mean. The same Gospel promises that “people will come from east and west, from north and south, and will eat in the kingdom of God.” Tomorrow, at the Jordan, Jesus himself goes down into the water and opens the door. Our ancestors kept this night with lights on plantain stems, crying El Paiya, God is light, and with a bath in river or pond recalling the Jordan. Tonight let us ask for the grace to enter by the door he opens.
outline: Ask: what do the lamps and the night bath of the Denha eve mean?
Strive to enter; guests come from east and west.
“Strive to enter through the narrow door.”
live: Keep the Denha eve
Light a lamp at home tonight and pray: Christ, light of the world, shine on our family.
A good work instead of an argument (Titus 3:8–9)
Leave aside one useless dispute and do one concrete good work instead.
2027-01-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, tomorrow you go down into the Jordan to open for us the door of life. Keep me from empty quarrels, make me eager for good works, and give me strength to enter through the narrow door into the feast of your kingdom. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is a foretaste of the banquet where people from east and west, north and south eat in the kingdom of God (Luke 13:29). We enter it through the door of Baptism.

2027-01-07.title: First Thursday of Denha
2027-01-07.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: A great prophet has risen among us
2027-01-07.verse: Fear seized all of them; and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has risen among us!” and “God has looked favorably on his people!”
theo: The day after Denha the Church goes on contemplating what God has revealed. St Paul speaks of a wisdom that is “not a wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age”, but “God's wisdom, secret and hidden, which God decreed before the ages for our glory.” The powerful did not grasp it; “if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” Now it has been opened to us. “What no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor the human heart conceived, what God has prepared for those who love him”, God has revealed “through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.”

In the Gospel this hidden wisdom shows its face. At the gate of Nain Jesus meets a funeral: a widow is burying “his mother's only son”. No one asks him for anything. Luke says simply that the Lord saw her and “had compassion for her”. He tells her not to weep, touches the bier and commands: “Young man, I say to you, rise!” Then “Jesus gave him to his mother”, the very gesture of Elijah at Zarephath. The crowd cries out: “A great prophet has risen among us!” and “God has looked favorably on his people!” In the season of Denha this is what manifestation means: the wisdom of God revealed as a compassion that stops at our funerals and gives life.
outline: Ask: where have you seen God's wisdom take the form of compassion?
Not the wisdom of this age.
Point 2 · What no eye has seen
Prepared for those who love him.
Compassion at the gate of Nain.
“God has looked favorably on his people!”
live: Ask for true wisdom (1 Corinthians 2:10)
Read one page of the Gospel slowly today and ask the Spirit to show you its depth.
Stop at a sorrow (Luke 7:13)
Visit or call someone who is grieving this week.
2027-01-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, wisdom of God made visible, you stopped at the gate of Nain and gave a widow back her son. Open my eyes by your Spirit to what God has prepared for those who love him, and give me your compassion for those who weep. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Lord of glory, whom the rulers of this age crucified, comes to us risen. He who said to the young man, rise, gives us the bread of eternal life.

2027-01-08.title: First Friday of Denha · Commemoration of St John the Baptist
2027-01-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Prepare the way of the Lord
John bore witness before the coming of Jesus
Paul, a prisoner for Christ and servant of the gospel
The martyrdom of John the Baptist
2027-01-08.alt: Season of Denha. The Third Qudasha is used today.
2027-01-08.verse: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.
theo: On the Fridays of Denha the Church honours the great witnesses who made Christ known. The first is John the Baptist, who saw the heavens open over Jesus at the Jordan. Isaiah had foretold his mission: a voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the way of the Lord, so that “the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, and all people shall see it together.” In the synagogue of Antioch in Pisidia St Paul tells the whole story of Israel, from Egypt to David, and then names the forerunner: “before his coming John had already proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.” And John himself said: “I am not he. No, but one is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of the sandals on his feet.”

John paid for his witness with his life. He told Herod plainly: “It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.” Herod feared him, “knowing that he was a righteous and holy man”, and even liked to listen to him; but at a birthday banquet, out of regard for his oaths and his guests, he sent a soldier to behead him in prison. Herod's power withered like grass; John's witness still speaks. “The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.” St Paul, himself “a prisoner for Christ Jesus”, shows what such witness builds: a household in which strangers become “citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone.” John, the last of the prophets, belongs to that foundation. The question he leaves us is simple: will I speak the truth with love, whatever it costs?
outline: Ask: when was the last time you said a hard truth with love?
Point 1 · A voice in the wilderness
The household of God, with Christ the cornerstone.
“The word of our God will stand forever.”
live: Speak the truth with love (Mark 6:18)
Correct one wrong gently and honestly, instead of keeping silent.
Pray for the persecuted
Pray today for Christians imprisoned or threatened for their faith, as John and Paul were.
2027-01-08.prayer: O God, you sent John the Baptist to prepare the way of your Son and to bear witness to the truth even to death. Give us his humility, to point always to Christ, and his courage, to speak the truth with love; and build us with all your saints into a dwelling place for you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Third Qudasha is used today. At the altar we unite ourselves with John, the prophets and the apostles, the foundation on which the household of God is built.

2027-01-09.title: First Saturday of Denha
2027-01-09.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The one whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world
2027-01-09.verse: But if I do them, even though you do not believe me, believe the works, so that you may know and understand that the Father is in me and I am in the Father.
theo: In the season of Denha the Church keeps asking: who is this Jesus revealed at the Jordan? In today's Gospel the question becomes dangerous. In the Temple the crowd picks up stones, and Jesus asks: “I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of these are you going to stone me?” They answer that it is for blasphemy, “because you, though only a human being, are making yourself God.” Jesus does not withdraw his claim. He is “the one whom the Father has sanctified and sent into the world”, and he points to his works: “believe the works, so that you may know and understand that the Father is in me and I am in the Father.” The voice at the Jordan said the same: this is my Son.

St Paul faces the same mystery from another side. Gentiles who were not seeking righteousness have received it, “that is, righteousness through faith”, while many in Israel, seeking it by works, “have stumbled over the stumbling stone”. Christ is that stone: for some a rock to trip over, for others a sure foundation, for “whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.” The same Jesus who is the light of Denha can become a stone we trip over, if we want to save ourselves on our own terms. Faith receives him as a gift.
outline: Ask: what makes it hard for people today to believe that Jesus is God?
A gift received, not a wage earned.
Christ, a rock to trip over or to build on.
The Father in the Son, the Son in the Father.
“The Father is in me and I am in the Father.”
live: Receive, do not earn (Romans 9:32)
Thank God today for one gift you did nothing to deserve.
Look at his works (John 10:38)
Write down one work of God you have seen in your life this past year.
2027-01-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, sanctified and sent into the world by the Father, you are in the Father and the Father is in you. Let me not stumble over you through pride, but build my life on you by faith, and let your works lead me to adore you as my Lord and my God. Amen.
altar: At every Holy Qurbana we profess that Jesus is God from God, Light from Light, one in being with the Father. Here the stone rejected by the builders becomes the cornerstone of our life.

2027-01-11.title: Second Monday of Denha
2027-01-11.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: When you come together as a church, there are divisions among you
That they may all be one
2027-01-11.verse: that they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
theo: At the Last Supper, before he goes out to his Passion, Jesus prays not only for the apostles but “also on behalf of those who will believe in me through their word”: that is, for us. And what does he ask? “That they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.” The unity of Christians is not a matter of good organisation; its source and model is the communion of the Father and the Son. And it has a missionary purpose: when Christians are one, the world can recognise that Jesus comes from the Father. Denha is the season of manifestation, and our unity is one of the ways in which Christ is still made manifest.

Paul shows us the opposite picture. In Corinth, “when you come together as a church, I hear that there are divisions among you”. At the very meal of the Lord the better-off eat their own supper first, and “one goes hungry and another becomes drunk”. Paul is blunt: “Do you show contempt for the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing?” To divide the Body at the table of the Body is a contradiction. Our parishes and families are not free of such divisions: rich and poor, old families and newcomers, groups that no longer speak to one another, quarrels even about holy things. Jesus' prayer is for us. The Holy Qurbana is the sacrament of unity, and we cannot receive it with a clear heart while we despise a brother or sister.
outline: Ask: what divides people in our parish or our family?
Point 2 · That they may all be one
Point 3 · So that the world may believe
live: Make peace before Qurbana (1 Corinthians 11:18)
Before you next go to Holy Qurbana, take one step towards someone you are divided from: a call, a greeting, a word of apology.
Pray Jesus' prayer (John 17:21)
Pray each day for the unity of all Christians, preparing for the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January).
2027-01-11.prayer: Lord Jesus, on the night before you suffered you prayed that we may all be one, as you and the Father are one. Heal the divisions in my family, my parish and your Church, and never let me despise a brother or sister at your table, so that the world may believe that the Father has sent you. Amen.
altar: Paul warns that division at the Lord's supper contradicts its very meaning. In the Holy Qurbana we exchange the peace before the Anaphora and pray for the peace and unity of the Church before we approach the one Bread.

2027-01-12.title: Second Tuesday of Denha
2027-01-12.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Abide in me; abide in my love
2027-01-12.verse: I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
theo: Yesterday Jesus prayed that we may be one; today the readings show what that unity looks like from the inside. Paul uses the image of the body: “For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ.” Notice that Paul does not end with the Church but with Christ himself: the Church is Christ's own Body, and we became its members in Baptism, for “in the one Spirit we were all baptized into one body”. No member may say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body.” The grandmother who prays her rosary quietly at the back, the catechism teacher, the young man who carries the processional cross: “God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.” Envy and self-contempt both forget this.

Jesus teaches the same truth with the image of the vine: “I am the vine, you are the branches.” Life flows from the vine into every branch; cut off, a branch withers. The Father is the vinegrower, and he prunes the fruitful branch “to make it bear more fruit”: our trials are often his pruning, not his rejection. Again and again in these verses Jesus says abide. It is the language of a home, of staying. “As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love.” We abide in him by keeping his word, by prayer, and above all in the Holy Qurbana, where he says to us once more: abide in me as I abide in you.
outline: Ask: what happens to a branch cut off from the plant?
Each of us belongs and is needed.
Staying with him through word, prayer and Qurbana.
“Apart from me you can do nothing.”
live: Honour another member (1 Corinthians 12:18)
Thank one person in your parish whose service usually goes unnoticed.
Abide in him (John 15:4)
Make one visit this week to Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament, simply to stay with him.
2027-01-12.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the vine and we are the branches. Keep me joined to you and to all the members of your Body. Prune in me whatever bears no fruit, and let me abide in your love, so that the Father may be glorified by the fruit of my life. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the many become one body, because all of us share the one Bread. Here the branches receive the life of the vine.

2027-01-13.title: Second Wednesday of Denha
2027-01-13.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: He is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one
Do you love me? Feed my sheep
2027-01-13.verse: For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.
theo: Paul asks the Gentile Christians of Ephesus to remember where they came from: “without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world.” That was the condition of our own ancestors before the Gospel reached these shores. “But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall.” In the Temple of Jerusalem a stone barrier kept Gentiles out of the inner courts. On the Cross Christ tore down every such wall, in order to “create in himself one new humanity in place of the two”. And so Paul concludes: “you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God”.

Who will care for this one household? In the Gospel the risen Lord, by the lake, asks Simon Peter three times: “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Only after each answer of love does he give the charge: feed my lambs, tend my sheep, feed my sheep. The flock never becomes Peter's property; Jesus still calls them my sheep. And the first qualification for caring for them is not talent or position but love for Christ. This touches each of us: parents who feed their children in the faith, teachers and catechists, priests and bishops, and the Successor of Peter. Then Jesus adds the hardest word: “Follow me.” Love for the Shepherd leads to laying down one's life for the sheep, as Peter himself would do in Rome.
outline: Ask: have you ever felt like an outsider? What made you feel at home?
The dividing wall broken down on the Cross.
Love for Christ before service of the flock.
live: Welcome a stranger (Ephesians 2:19)
Greet and welcome someone new or alone at church this Sunday.
Serve out of love (John 21:15–17)
Before each service you give this week, at home or in the parish, say quietly: Lord, you know that I love you.
2027-01-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are our peace. By your blood you brought near those who were far off and broke down the walls that divide us. Make me a member of your household who welcomes others, and give me a love for you that shows itself in caring for your sheep. Amen.
altar: At the altar the near and the far, rich and poor, people of every language are reconciled to God in one body through the Cross. The Holy Qurbana is offered in communion with the Pope and our bishops, the shepherds to whom Christ has entrusted his sheep.

2027-01-14.title: Second Thursday of Denha · St Devasahayam
2027-01-14.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you
Even the wind and the sea obey him
2027-01-14.alt: Season of Denha. St Devasahayam, martyr: Romans 9:30–33; John 10:31–39.
2027-01-14.verse: Resist him, steadfast in your faith, for you know that your brothers and sisters in all the world are undergoing the same kinds of suffering.
theo: At evening, after a long day of teaching, Jesus says to his disciples: “Let us go across to the other side.” On the lake “a great windstorm arose, and the waves beat into the boat”, while Jesus is “in the stern, asleep on the cushion”. The frightened disciples wake him: “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?” He rises, rebukes the wind and says to the sea: “Peace! Be still!” Then comes the question for every age of the Church: “Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?” The disciples are left wondering: “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?” This is a true Denha: the one asleep in their boat is the Lord of creation, the God who “made the storm be still” (Psalm 107:29).

Peter, who was in that boat, later writes to Christians facing persecution: “Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.” The disciples' cry, do you not care, receives its answer: he cares. But Peter is realistic: “Like a roaring lion your adversary the devil prowls around, looking for someone to devour. Resist him, steadfast in your faith.” Today the Church in India honours St Devasahayam, who lived this word. Born Neelakanta Pillai, an official in the service of the kingdom of Travancore, he was baptised in 1745 and took the name Lazarus, Devasahayam. After his Baptism he refused to treat anyone as untouchable; for his faith he was arrested, paraded through towns and kept in chains for nearly three years, and at Aralvaimozhy in 1752 he was shot dead. The storm did not cease for him on earth, but Christ was in his boat, and his faith did not fail. The first reading of his memorial says it: “whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.”
outline: Ask: what storm are you in right now?
Jesus, Lord of wind and sea.
Point 2 · Cast all your anxiety on him
St Devasahayam, faithful in the storm.
“Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?”
live: Hand over one worry (1 Peter 5:7)
Write down your heaviest worry today, offer it to Jesus in prayer or at Holy Qurbana, and say: you care for me.
Pray for persecuted Christians
Through the prayers of St Devasahayam, pray for Christians in India and elsewhere who suffer for their faith.
2027-01-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, you slept in the boat and rose to command the wind and the sea. When storms rise in my life, let me cast all my anxiety on you, because you care for me. Through the prayers of St Devasahayam, who stayed steadfast in faith through chains and death, keep me firm and unashamed in confessing you. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is the Lord's presence in the boat of the Church. The Body of Christ that St Devasahayam received is the strength of martyrs and the peace of the anxious.

2027-01-15.title: Second Friday of Denha · Commemoration of Sts Peter and Paul, the Apostles
2027-01-15.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Elisha brings the Shunammite's son back to life
You are the Messiah; you are Peter
2027-01-15.alt: Season of Denha. The calendar joins John 21:15–19 to the Gospel.
2027-01-15.verse: And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
theo: On the Fridays of Denha the Church honours the great witnesses who made Christ known. Today we keep the memory of Peter and Paul. At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asks: “Who do people say that the Son of Man is?” The answers are generous but too small: John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah, one of the prophets. Then comes the question no one else can answer for us: “But who do you say that I am?” Simon answers: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.” This is a moment of Denha, for Jesus says: “flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father in heaven.” On this faith, and on the man who confessed it, Christ builds: “you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.” He gives him the keys of the kingdom and the power to bind and to loose. The ministry of Peter continues in the Pope, the Successor of Peter, who strengthens his brothers and sisters in this same confession.

The other readings show the apostles carrying the life of Christ into the world. In Joppa the disciple Tabitha, who “was devoted to good works and acts of charity”, falls ill and dies, and the widows show Peter the tunics she had made for them. Peter puts everyone outside, kneels and prays, and says: “Tabitha, get up.” She opens her eyes. Long before, Elisha had raised the Shunammite woman's son after praying behind a closed door; now Peter raises a daughter of the Church in the name of the risen Jesus, and “many believed in the Lord”. Paul, for his part, lists what his apostleship cost him: “Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I received a stoning. Three times I was shipwrecked”, and on top of all this, “my anxiety for all the churches”. He boasts only of his weakness. Peter the rock and Paul the weak one, both martyred in Rome: through them the same Lord gives life and builds his Church.
outline: Ask: if Jesus asked you today, “But who do you say that I am?”, what would you answer?
Point 1 · Who do you say that I am?
Peter's confession, revealed by the Father.
The Church built on Peter; the keys of the kingdom.
The apostles carry the life of the risen Lord.
Point 4 · I will boast of my weakness
“You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
live: Make Peter's confession (Matthew 16:16)
Each morning this week say slowly: Jesus, you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.
Pray for the Pope
Pray today for the Pope, the Successor of Peter, and for our Major Archbishop and bishops.
2027-01-15.prayer: Lord Jesus, Messiah and Son of the living God, you built your Church on the rock of Peter and sent Paul to the nations through many sufferings. Through their prayers keep me firm in confessing you, generous in good works like Tabitha, and faithful in my weakness. Bless our Holy Father the Pope and all our shepherds. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is offered in communion with the Pope, the Successor of Peter, and with our bishops. At the altar we make Peter's confession our own: you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.

2027-01-16.title: Second Saturday of Denha
2027-01-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Faith comes from what is heard
2027-01-16.verse: So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.
theo: In the synagogue of Capernaum the people are “astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.” The scribes quoted the teachers before them; Jesus speaks as the one whose word does what it says. A man with an unclean spirit cries out: “What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are, the Holy One of God.” Jesus rebukes the spirit: “Be silent, and come out of him!” and the man is set free. The crowd asks: “What is this? A new teaching, with authority!” In Denha we see that the word of Jesus is not mere advice but power: it drives out evil and makes people whole.

Paul explains how this word reaches every nation: “For one believes with the heart and so is justified, and one confesses with the mouth and so is saved.” And “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.” But no one can call on a Lord of whom they have never heard. Paul asks: “And how are they to proclaim him unless they are sent?” and answers with Isaiah: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!” Then he sums it up: “So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.” Our own faith came by hearing, through apostles, missionaries, parents and catechists who were sent. Now it is our turn: to open our mouths for Christ, to support those who are sent, and to let our feet carry the good news.
outline: Ask: who first told you about Jesus?
The heart and the mouth together.
Faith comes from what is heard, so someone must be sent.
“So faith comes from what is heard.”
live: Confess with your mouth (Romans 10:10)
Speak about your faith to one person this week, simply and gently.
Support those who are sent (Romans 10:15)
Pray for a missionary, and give something to the mission work of your diocese.
2027-01-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, you teach with authority and your word drives out every evil. Let your word live in my heart and on my lips; free me from all that binds me, and make my feet beautiful in carrying your good news to others. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the word of Christ is first proclaimed and heard, and then he gives himself on the altar. The Lord who commanded the unclean spirit comes to dwell in us.

2027-01-18.title: Third Monday of Denha · First Day of the Three Days' Fast
2027-01-18.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: God, the LORD, is my strength
Forgive your brother or sister from your heart
2027-01-18.alt: Season of Denha. Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu, the Rogation of the Ninevites). Church Unity Octave begins (Ephesians 4:1–6; John 17:6–11).
2027-01-18.verse: Yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
theo: Today begins the Three Days' Fast, the Rogation of the Ninevites, born in a time of plague when the Church of the East fasted and begged God for mercy. The first reading gives us the words for such a prayer. A people back from exile looks at its ruins and cries: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down”. They do not pretend: “all our righteous deeds are like a filthy cloth. We all fade like a leaf”. Yet they hold on to one truth: “Yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter”, and they plead: “do not remember iniquity forever. Now consider, we are all your people.” Habakkuk adds the faith that keeps praying even when the fields are bare: “Though the fig tree does not blossom… yet I will rejoice in the LORD”.

Paul urges that “supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone”, even for kings and rulers, because God “desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.” A rogation is exactly this: the Church praying for the whole world. But Jesus warns that a prayer for mercy is empty if we refuse mercy. The servant released from a debt of ten thousand talents seizes a fellow servant by the throat over a hundred denarii. The master asks: “Should you not have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you?” And Jesus says the Father will deal so with us “if you do not forgive your brother or sister from your heart.” Our fast begins with forgiveness. Today the Unity Octave also begins: Christians who ask God not to remember their sins must learn to forgive one another.
outline: Ask: what would you say to God if you saw your town in ruins?
Isaiah's honest prayer: you are our Father.
God desires all to be saved.
The servant forgiven much who would not forgive little.
“Yet, O LORD, you are our Father.”
live: Fast with the Ninevites
Keep the fast today as your health allows: one simple meal, no snacks, no meat.
Forgive one debt (Matthew 18:35)
Name one person you have not forgiven and forgive him or her from your heart today, in prayer and, if possible, in deed.
2027-01-18.prayer: Merciful Father, we are the clay and you are our potter. As we begin the fast of the Ninevites, do not remember our iniquity forever. Teach us to pray for everyone, and give us hearts that forgive as we have been forgiven. Make all Christians one in your mercy. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Church prays for the whole world, for rulers and for all peoples, as Paul asks; and we approach the altar only after forgiving our brother and sister.

2027-01-19.title: Third Tuesday of Denha · Second Day of the Three Days' Fast
2027-01-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Return to the LORD with all your heart
Your iniquities have been barriers between you and your God
Be transformed by the renewing of your minds
The Pharisee and the tax collector
2027-01-19.alt: Season of Denha. Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu, the Rogation of the Ninevites). Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-19.verse: But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even look up to heaven, but was beating his breast and saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
theo: On the second day of the fast the readings show what a true fast looks like. At Mizpah Samuel tells Israel: “If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods”. The people draw water and pour it out before the LORD, fast all day and confess: “We have sinned against the LORD.” When the Philistines attack, they beg Samuel: “Do not cease to cry out to the LORD our God for us”, and Samuel prays, “and the LORD answered him.” Isaiah explains why prayer can seem unheard: “See, the LORD’s hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. Rather, your iniquities have been barriers between you and your God”. Fasting is the work of taking those barriers down.

Then Jesus shows two men at prayer. The Pharisee is a serious religious man: “I fast twice a week; I give a tenth of all my income.” But he prays “standing by himself”, comparing himself with “this tax collector”. The tax collector stands far off and says only: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” It is he who goes home justified, “for all who exalt themselves will be humbled, but all who humble themselves will be exalted.” Paul shows the fruit of such humility: we offer our bodies “as a living sacrifice”, we are “transformed by the renewing of your minds”, and we learn “not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think”, because “we, who are many, are one body in Christ”. A fast that makes us proud is the Pharisee's fast; a fast that makes us humble and one with others is the fast God accepts.
