In this Unity Octave, the tax collector's prayer is also the prayer of divided Christians.
outline: Ask: can someone fast, pray and give to the Church, and still go home without God's mercy?
Point 1 · Return with all your heart
Mizpah: idols put away, water poured out, sin confessed.
God's hand is not too short; our sins stand in between.
The proud fast and the humble prayer.
“God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”
live: Pray the tax collector's prayer (Luke 18:13)
Repeat it slowly throughout the day, especially when you feel hungry.
Put away one idol (1 Samuel 7:3)
Remove one thing that stands between you and God: an app, a habit, a resentment.
2027-01-19.prayer: Lord God, your hand is not too short to save. Take away the barriers our sins have raised between us and you. Keep us from the pride that fasts and despises others; give us the heart of the tax collector, and transform us by the renewing of our minds, one body in Christ. God, be merciful to us, sinners. Amen.
altar: At the beginning of the Holy Qurbana we confess that we are sinners and ask for mercy. We come like the tax collector, and offer ourselves with Christ as a living sacrifice.

2027-01-20.title: Third Wednesday of Denha · Third Day of the Three Days' Fast · St Sebastian
2027-01-20.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Sanctify a fast; spare your people, O LORD
The fasting and prayer of Nineveh
God shows mercy: objects of mercy from every people
Your Father who sees in secret will reward you
2027-01-20.alt: Season of Denha. Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu, the Rogation of the Ninevites). St Sebastian, martyr, and the name day of Mar Sebastian Vadakkel, Mar Sebastian Adayanthrath, Mar Sebastian Vaniyapurackal and Mar Sebastian Pozholiparampil. The Third Qudasha (Anaphora of Mar Nestorius) is used today. Readings for St Sebastian: Deuteronomy 32:37–43; Isaiah 49:1–4; 2 Timothy 2:1–5; Matthew 10:24–33.
2027-01-20.verse: When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity that he had said he would bring upon them; and he did not do it.
theo: On the last day of the fast we read the story that gave it its name. Jonah walks into the great city with a short warning: “Forty days more, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!” And “the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.” The king leaves his throne, sits in ashes and says: “Who knows? God may relent and change his mind”. “When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity”. Joel shows the same scene in Jerusalem: “Blow the trumpet in Zion; sanctify a fast; call a solemn assembly”; gather the old and the children, “even infants at the breast”, and let the priests weep between the vestibule and the altar: “Spare your people, O LORD”. Then “the LORD became jealous for his land, and had pity on his people.” This is Moonnu Nombu: a whole people, young and old, together before the altar.

Paul uses the image of the potter to say that all depends on God's mercy, and that he gathers “objects of mercy” not only from Israel but from the Gentiles: “Those who were not my people I will call ‘my people’”. Nineveh, a pagan city that repented, was an early sign of it. Jesus adds a warning so that our fast does not end in a show: “Beware of practicing your piety before others in order to be seen by them”. When we give alms, the left hand must not know what the right hand is doing, and “your Father who sees in secret will reward you.” Today we also honour St Sebastian, much loved in Kerala, and pray for our bishops who bear his name. Tradition remembers him as an officer who quietly strengthened Christians in prison before he confessed Christ openly with his blood. Let our fast end with mercy done in secret and faith confessed without fear.
outline: Ask: when did you last see a whole parish, from grandparents to babies, gathered to pray for mercy?
Joel: everyone gathered; the priests weep at the altar.
Point 2 · Who knows? God may relent
Nineveh turns, and God has pity.
Point 3 · In secret, and without fear
Alms in secret; St Sebastian's quiet service and bold witness.
“God changed his mind… and he did not do it.”
live: Give alms in secret (Matthew 6:3)
Give what you saved by fasting to someone in need, and tell no one.
Honour St Sebastian
Pray for our bishops named Sebastian and for all soldiers and police.
2027-01-20.prayer: Merciful God, when Nineveh fasted and turned from evil, you had pity and did not do the evil you had threatened. Look on your people at the end of these three days; spare us, Lord, and make us objects of your mercy. Teach us to do good in secret, and through the prayers of St Sebastian make us brave in confessing your name. Amen.
altar: Joel's priests wept between the vestibule and the altar. At the Holy Qurbana the priest still stands there for us, pleading: spare your people, O Lord.

2027-01-21.title: Third Thursday of Denha · Thursday after the Three Days' Fast
2027-01-21.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked
Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity?
No greater joy than to hear that my children walk in the truth
Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents
2027-01-21.alt: Season of Denha. Thanksgiving after the Three Days' Fast. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-21.verse: Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
theo: The fast is over, and the Church celebrates the joy of God who forgives. Ezekiel hears God swear: “As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live.” Micah sings: “Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity…? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in showing clemency… You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.” After three days of turning, we hear God's answer: mercy.

In the Gospel tax collectors and sinners come near to Jesus, and the Pharisees grumble. Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one lost sheep, and of a woman who sweeps her house to find one lost coin. When they find them, they call their neighbours: “Rejoice with me.” “Just so… there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.” John the Elder writes: “I have no greater joy than this, to hear that my children are walking in the truth.” The fruit of the fast is joy: God's joy over us, and our joy in walking in his truth.
outline: Ask: have you ever found something precious you had lost?
Micah's God who delights in mercy.
“Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.”
live: Rejoice in mercy
Thank God tonight for the graces of the three days.
Seek the lost (Luke 15:4)
Contact one person who has drifted from you or from the Church.
2027-01-21.prayer: God of mercy, you take no pleasure in the death of sinners and you cast our sins into the depths of the sea. Thank you for the grace of these days of fasting. Let us share heaven's joy over every sinner who returns, and walk always in your truth. Amen.
altar: Each Qurbana is a feast of the found: we were lost, and the Shepherd carries us home on his shoulders to his table.

2027-01-22.title: Third Friday of Denha · Commemoration of the Evangelists
2027-01-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Signs and wonders through the apostles
In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel
2027-01-22.alt: Season of Denha. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-22.verse: For though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
theo: On the third Friday of Denha the Church honours the four Evangelists, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, through whom the good news has reached every land. The readings show what the Gospel is: God making himself known. On Mount Carmel Elijah repairs the broken altar with twelve stones, “according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob”, soaks the offering with water and prays: “Answer me, O LORD, answer me, so that this people may know that you, O LORD, are God, and that you have turned their hearts back.” Fire falls, and the whole people cries: “The LORD indeed is God; the LORD indeed is God.” This is Denha: the true God revealed. In Acts the same God works “many signs and wonders” through the apostles, and the sick are laid in the streets so “that Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them”.

In the Gospel Jesus calls the Twelve by name; among them are “James son of Zebedee, and his brother John” and “Thomas and Matthew the tax collector”. He sends them out: “As you go, proclaim the good news, ‘The kingdom of heaven has come near.’” And he adds: “You received without payment; give without payment.” The Evangelists did in writing what the Twelve did by voice: Matthew and John from among the Twelve, Mark and Luke from the circle of Peter and Paul. Paul tells the Corinthians what it cost: “We are fools for the sake of Christ”, hungry, homeless, reviled; yet “in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.” Through their four books the Evangelists are fathers in faith to us too. In Kerala the faith first preached by the Apostle Thomas has been fed for centuries by these Gospels, read at every Holy Qurbana.
outline: Ask: who first told you about Jesus? Who is your father or mother in the faith?
Point 1 · The LORD indeed is God
Elijah's altar, the fire, the people's cry.
The Twelve sent; signs through the apostles.
The Evangelists and Paul: the cost and the fruit.
“In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.”
live: Read a Gospel
Begin reading one Gospel through, a chapter a day.
Give without payment (Matthew 10:8)
Share one gift of time or skill freely this week, expecting nothing back.
2027-01-22.prayer: Lord Jesus, you sent the Twelve to proclaim that the kingdom of heaven has come near, and through the four Evangelists your Gospel has reached us. Let the fire of your Spirit fall on our hearts, so that we may say with all your people: the Lord indeed is God. Make us glad to give freely what we have freely received. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Gospel book is carried in honour and Christ speaks when it is read. Then the Holy Spirit is invoked on the offerings: the fire Elijah prayed for comes upon our altar.

2027-01-23.title: Third Saturday of Denha
2027-01-23.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Striving side by side for the faith of the gospel
The faith of the Canaanite woman
2027-01-23.alt: Season of Denha. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-23.verse: Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed instantly.
theo: Paul writes to the Philippians from prison with one wish: “live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ”, so that he may hear that they are “standing firm in one spirit, striving side by side with one mind for the faith of the gospel, and are in no way intimidated by your opponents.” He even calls suffering a gift: “he has graciously granted you the privilege not only of believing in Christ, but of suffering for him as well”. In this Unity Octave his words are a plan for all Christians: not rivals, but companions side by side for the one Gospel.

The Gospel shows a faith that will not give up. A Canaanite woman, a foreigner, cries: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is tormented by a demon.” Jesus does not answer; the disciples want her sent away; Jesus says he was sent to the lost sheep of Israel. She kneels: “Lord, help me.” Even the hard saying about the children's food does not stop her: “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.” Jesus replies: “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” Denha celebrates Christ revealed to the nations; here a pagan mother teaches the disciples what faith looks like: humble, persistent, and sure that a crumb from Christ is enough.
outline: Ask: have you ever kept asking God when the answer seemed to be no?
A life that matches what we believe.
One spirit, one mind, one Gospel.

Choose one intention and bring it to Jesus every day this week: Lord, help me.
Side by side (Philippians 1:27)
During this Unity Octave, pray with or for a Christian of another Church.
2027-01-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. Give us the faith of the Canaanite woman, humble and persistent, and help us to live in a manner worthy of your Gospel, standing firm in one spirit with all who believe in you. Amen.
altar: Like the Canaanite woman we come to the Holy Qurbana knowing we are unworthy, and Christ gives us not crumbs but himself, the Bread of Life.

2027-01-25.title: Fourth Monday of Denha · Conversion of Saint Paul
2027-01-25.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: God calls Moses from the burning bush
He appeared also to me, as to one untimely born
2027-01-25.alt: Season of Denha. Conversion of St Paul. The Church Unity Octave concludes. Weekday readings of the day: Acts 16:25–34; Luke 5:12–16.
2027-01-25.verse: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me has not been in vain. On the contrary, I worked harder than any of them—though it was not I, but the grace of God that is with me.
theo: Today's readings set two great calls side by side. Moses, a fugitive shepherd in the desert, sees a bush that burns and is not consumed, and hears his name: “Moses, Moses!” God reveals himself: “I AM WHO I AM.” Saul, a zealous persecutor on the road, is thrown to the ground by a light from heaven and hears his name: “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” He asks, “Who are you, Lord?” and hears: “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.” The God of the burning bush has a human face and a name, and he identifies himself with his suffering Church.

Saul is led blind into Damascus. Ananias, frightened but obedient, lays hands on him; “something like scales fell from his eyes, and his sight was restored.” He is baptized, and “immediately he began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, saying, ‘He is the Son of God.’” Years later Paul looks back with humility: Christ appeared to Cephas, to the Twelve, to more than five hundred, to James, “Last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me. For I am the least of the apostles.” And then the great sentence: “by the grace of God I am what I am.”

The Gospel explains this grace. The owner of the vineyard hires workers at dawn, at nine, at noon, at three, and even at five o'clock, and pays them all the same. Those hired first grumble. He answers: “Am I not allowed to do what I choose with what belongs to me? Or are you envious because I am generous?” Paul was hired at the eleventh hour, and received the full wage of grace. None of us earns salvation; all of us receive it. This is the good news for every latecomer, and the end of all envy in the Church.

The weekday readings carry the same grace further. In a Philippian prison at midnight Paul himself, the converted persecutor, is singing hymns when an earthquake opens the doors; the trembling jailer asks, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”, and Paul answers, “Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.” That same night the whole family is baptized. In Luke a man covered with leprosy begs, “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean”, and Jesus touches him: “I do choose. Be made clean.” The grace that met Saul on the road keeps finding the latecomers and the outcasts.
conn: Two calls by name.
“Moses, Moses” (Exodus 3:4) and “Saul, Saul” (Acts 9:4): the double name marks a decisive call.
I AM.
The divine name revealed at the bush is echoed in Jesus' words, “I am Jesus” (Acts 9:5).
Scales from the eyes.
A sign of baptismal enlightenment; the early Church called Baptism “illumination”.
Untimely born.
Paul's image for his late and unexpected call; grace overturns ordinary timing.
The eleventh hour.
Workers hired at five o'clock receive a full day's wage; the Fathers saw here the Gentiles and late converts.
Unity Octave.
Ends today: the apostle who once divided now unites.
The weekday readings.
Acts 16:25–34 and Luke 5:12–16: the jailer of Philippi and the leper show the same unearned grace that called Saul.
altar: Paul's sight was restored, then he was baptized and ate (Acts 9:18–19). Baptism leads to the table of the Qurbana.
At the altar no one is paid by merit; all receive the same Lord, by grace.

2027-01-25.prayer: Lord God, you appeared to Moses in the burning bush and to Saul on the road to Damascus. By your grace make us what you want us to be, free us from envy at your generosity, and through the prayers of St Paul unite all Christians in one faith. Glory to you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-26.title: Fourth Tuesday of Denha · Republic Day of India
2027-01-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: No prophet is accepted in the prophet's hometown
2027-01-26.alt: Season of Denha. Republic Day of India. Sts Timothy and Titus: 2 Samuel 22:2–4; Wisdom 7:28–8:3; 1 Timothy 6:11–16; Matthew 16:24–27.
2027-01-26.verse: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
theo: Hebrews looks back at Israel in the wilderness, who heard God's promise of rest and did not enter it, “because they were not united by faith with those who listened.” The promise has not expired: “while the promise of entering his rest is still open, let us take care that none of you should seem to have failed to reach it.” And God sets a day for us, the same day every day: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.” The Gospel shows what a hardened heart looks like. In the synagogue at Nazareth everyone at first speaks well of Jesus and is amazed at his gracious words; then comes the question, “Is not this Joseph's son?” Familiarity turns to contempt. Jesus answers, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in the prophet's hometown”, and reminds them that Elijah was sent to a widow in Sidon and Elisha cleansed Naaman the Syrian. God's mercy crosses borders. The townspeople are filled with rage and try to throw him off a cliff, “But he passed through the midst of them and went on his way.”

Today India keeps Republic Day, remembering the Constitution that came into force in 1950, promising justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all and the freedom to profess, practise and propagate religion. The Gospel speaks to such a day. It is easy to love one's own town and harder to hear the prophet who comes from it; easy to think God belongs to us and harder to rejoice that he blesses the widow of Zarephath and the Syrian general. Christians serve their nation best by listening today to God's voice, by refusing contempt for those they know too well, and by welcoming every neighbour of every faith. The Church also honours Sts Timothy and Titus, the young bishops whom Paul trusted with the churches of Ephesus and Crete. To Timothy he wrote: “Fight the good fight of the faith”. We give thanks for our country, pray for all who govern it, and ask for pastors who, like Timothy and Titus, keep the faith among the people.

Point 1 · Today, if you hear his voice
The rest still open; do not harden your hearts.
Point 2 · Is not this Joseph's son?
Zarephath, Naaman, and a nation of many faiths.
“Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”

2027-01-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, in your own hometown you were not accepted, yet you passed through the crowd and went on your way to save us. Soften our hearts to hear your voice today. On this Republic Day bless India with justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, make us good citizens and faithful disciples, and through the prayers of Sts Timothy and Titus give your Church shepherds who fight the good fight of the faith. Amen.
altar: At every Holy Qurbana we hear his voice today in the word, pray for those who govern, as the Church has always done, and receive the rest he promised in his Body and Blood.

2027-01-27.title: Fourth Wednesday of Denha
2027-01-27.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: There is only the gospel of Christ
He calls his own sheep by name
2027-01-27.verse: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep hear his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
theo: In Galatians Paul skips the thanksgiving with which he usually greets a church and goes straight to his alarm: “I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting the one who called you in the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel.” Then he corrects himself: “not that there is another gospel.” There is only one Gospel, because there is only one Christ. Some were telling the Galatians that grace was not enough, that they must add the old observances to be saved. Paul answers with fierce words, because to change the Gospel is to lose Christ. And he examines his own heart: “Am I now seeking human approval, or God's approval? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be a servant of Christ.” A preacher who tells people only what they want to hear has stopped serving the Lord.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of the sheepfold. Thieves and bandits climb in another way; the shepherd comes through the gate, and “the sheep hear his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.” The sheep “will not follow a stranger”, because they do not know the voice of strangers. Here is the answer to the confusion in Galatia: the Church is kept in the truth not by clever arguments but by knowing the Shepherd's voice. That voice is learned by long listening, in Scripture, in the Holy Qurbana, in the teaching handed on by the apostles. Denha reveals a Shepherd who is not distant: he knows each of us by name, goes ahead of us, and leads us out.
outline: Ask: how many voices tried to guide you today?
Grace is not something we add to.
Point 3 · He calls his sheep by name
“He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.”

2027-01-27.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, good Shepherd, you call each of us by name and lead us out. Keep us faithful to the one Gospel we have received, free us from the desire to please people more than God, and teach us to know your voice and follow you. Amen.
altar: At every Holy Qurbana the Shepherd's voice is heard in the Gospel, and the flock he calls by name is fed at his table.

2027-01-28.title: Fourth Thursday of Denha · St Thomas Aquinas
2027-01-28.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The love of Christ urges us on
The call of the first disciples
2027-01-28.alt: Season of Denha. St Thomas Aquinas: 1 Kings 3:5–12; Wisdom 7:7–14; 1 Corinthians 1:18–25; Matthew 5:13–16.
2027-01-28.verse: For the love of Christ urges us on, because we are convinced that one has died for all; therefore all have died.
theo: Paul explains to the Corinthians what drives him. Some boast “in outward appearance and not in the heart”; he has a different motive: “For the love of Christ urges us on, because we are convinced that one has died for all; therefore all have died.” Christ's love is not only something Paul feels for Christ; it is Christ's own love for him, pressing on him like a current, carrying him toward others. In the Gospel that love begins with a glance and a question. John the Baptist sees Jesus walking by and exclaims, “Look, here is the Lamb of God!” Two disciples follow. Jesus turns and asks them, “What are you looking for?” They answer with another question, calling him Rabbi, Teacher: “where are you staying?” He says, “Come and see.” They stay with him that day; John even remembers the hour, about four o'clock in the afternoon. Andrew then finds his brother: “We have found the Messiah”, and Jesus looks at Simon and gives him a new name, Cephas. Denha shows us how Christ is made known: one person tells another, and Christ himself does the rest.

Today the Church honours St Thomas Aquinas, the Dominican friar whose great mind served the faith. He taught that reason can prepare the way, but only faith receives the truth that Christ is the Son of God, and he wrote that grace does not destroy nature but perfects it. His whole work answered Jesus' first question, “What are you looking for?” According to the early accounts of his life, he heard the Lord ask him in prayer what reward he wanted for all he had written, and he answered: nothing but you, Lord. Near the end of his life, after an experience at the Holy Qurbana, he stopped writing and said that all he had written seemed like straw beside what he had seen. Like the first disciples, he came, saw, and remained. The love of Christ urged him on.

Point 2 · What are you looking for?

2027-01-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Lamb of God, you asked your first disciples what they were looking for and invited them to come and see. 2027-01-29.title: Fourth Friday of Denha · Commemoration of St Stephen, Protomartyr
2027-01-29.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Carrying in the body the death of Jesus
2027-01-29.verse: always carrying in the body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our bodies.
theo: On the Fridays of Denha the Church remembers those through whom Christ was made visible, and today it is Stephen, the first martyr. The first reading tells of another innocent man. Naboth will not sell his family vineyard to King Ahab: “The LORD forbid that I should give you my ancestral inheritance.” Queen Jezebel arranges a religious fast, seats two scoundrels opposite Naboth to accuse him of cursing God and the king, and has him stoned outside the city. Then Elijah meets Ahab in the stolen vineyard with God's question: “Have you killed, and also taken possession?” In the Gospel Jesus laments over a city that repeats this story: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!” He speaks of all the righteous blood shed on earth, “from the blood of righteous Abel” onward.

Stephen stands at the end of that line, but he does not die as a victim only. Filled with the Holy Spirit, “he gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.” As the stones fall he prays, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit”, and kneeling, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” At his feet the witnesses lay their coats, beside a young man named Saul. Paul, once that young man, later describes the martyr's life from the inside: “We are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not driven to despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed; always carrying in the body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our bodies.” The stones were real, but so was the glory: “this slight momentary affliction is preparing us for an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure, because we look not at what can be seen but at what cannot be seen.” In Denha Stephen shows us Christ: the face of a forgiving God, visible in a dying man.
outline: Ask: what do you see when life throws stones at you?
The hen and her brood; Christ's lament.
Stephen sees the glory and forgives.
The life of Jesus made visible in us.
“The life of Jesus may also be made visible in our bodies.”

2027-01-29.prayer: Lord Jesus, standing at the right hand of God, you opened the heavens to your servant Stephen as he died forgiving his killers. Through his prayers, keep us from being crushed in affliction, let your life be made visible in our bodies, and give us the grace to say: Lord, do not hold this sin against them. Amen.
altar: At the altar we receive the life of Jesus under the signs of his death, so that we too may carry his death in our bodies and show his life.

2027-01-30.title: Fourth Saturday of Denha
2027-01-30.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Those who are born of God do not sin
Whoever is from God hears the words of God
2027-01-30.verse: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know him who is true; and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life.
theo: John ends his first letter by telling us why he wrote it: “so that you may know that you have eternal life.” Christians are not meant to live in anxious guessing. We have “boldness” before God: “if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.” Then John gives a surprising example of such prayer: praying for a brother or sister who sins. He distinguishes sin that is mortal from sin that is not, the distinction the Church still teaches between mortal and venial sin, and urges us to intercede so that God “will give life” to the one who has fallen. “We know that those who are born of God do not sin”: not that they never stumble, but that they do not make sin their home, because the Son of God protects them. The letter closes with a revelation fit for Denha, “He is the true God and eternal life”, and a final warning: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.”

In the Gospel Jesus' hearers claim a famous ancestry: “Abraham is our father.” Jesus answers that children resemble their father: “If you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did.” Abraham believed and welcomed God's messengers; they are planning to kill the one who tells them the truth. Belonging to God is not a matter of birth certificate but of listening: “Whoever is from God hears the words of God.” The devil, Jesus says, “is a liar and the father of lies.” Every lie we tell, every half-truth we live by, is a small idol. Saturday, the eve of the Lord's Day, is a good day to ask whose children we resemble, to pray for one another's sins, and to prepare for Sunday through the sacrament of Reconciliation.

Confidence in prayer and eternal life.

The hidden God has made himself known in his only Son.
Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ, and we are his house.
2027-01-10.action: Each morning this week pray: Arise, O Lord, go before me today.
2027-01-10.question: Do I let Christ go before me on the road, or do I walk alone?
kidsaint: The beloved disciple wrote that the Word became flesh and lived among us. Lesson: Jesus came to live close to us, and he wants to live in your heart too.
term: The eternal Son of God took a human nature and became man without ceasing to be God (John 1:14; CCC 461–463).

family.explain: God's Son came to live with us as a real man, Jesus. Through him we receive gift after gift from God.
family.intention: We pray that Jesus may live in our home and walk with us every day.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift from God did you receive today?”

illus: An illustration

A nurse from Kottayam working in a hospital in Kuwait keeps a small crucifix and a copy of St John's Gospel in her locker. When a colleague asked why, she answered: our God did not stay far away; he came to live where we live. So even here, far from home, I am not alone.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, eternal Word made flesh, you pitched your tent among us. Walk with us as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: Whenever the ark set out, Moses prayed: Arise, O Lord (Numbers 10:35). Do I let God go before me?
Truly, you are a God who hides himself (Isaiah 45:15). Where has God seemed hidden in my life?
From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace (John 1:16). Which graces can I name today?
pm.resp: Lord, go before us.
interc: For the Church, God's house, that she may hold firm her hope.
For migrants and travellers, that they may know God walks with them.
For those who find God hidden, that they may see his face in Jesus.
For our families, that Christ may dwell in our homes.
For our group, that we may receive grace upon grace.
pm.close: Father, your Word became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth. Make us his faithful house and lead us on the road to your glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses could not carry the people alone; God shared his Spirit.
Idols must be carried; the LORD carries his people.
Jesus is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
2027-01-17.action: Plan how you will keep the Three Days' Fast from tomorrow.
2027-01-17.question: What burden am I trying to carry alone that I should hand to the Lamb of God?
kidsaint: He lived in the desert and baptized people in the Jordan. When he saw Jesus he pointed and said: here is the Lamb of God! Lesson: our job is to point others to Jesus.
2027-01-17.special: Third Sunday of Denha. Moonnu Nombu and the Church Unity Octave begin tomorrow.
term: John the Baptist's name for Jesus (John 1:29). Like the Passover lamb, Jesus gives his life so that we are set free from sin; he takes away the sin of the world.

family.explain: John the Baptist saw Jesus coming and said: look, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world! Jesus carries away our sins, and he carries us too.
family.intention: We pray for our family as we begin the Three Days' Fast tomorrow.
family.ask: Ask: “What heavy thing can we ask Jesus to carry for us this week?”

illus: An illustration

An old man in Changanassery cared for his wife for eleven years after her stroke. Asked how he managed, he said: in the first year I tried to carry her alone and I broke. Then my sons took turns, the parish sent people, and I began to pray Isaiah 46 every morning. Now God carries both of us, and I only carry her cup of tea.

pm.open: Lord our God, you have carried us from our birth. As we gather, take our burdens and prepare our hearts for the fast. Amen.
share: “I am not able to carry all this people alone” (Numbers 11:14). What am I trying to carry alone?
“I will carry and will save” (Isaiah 46:4). Do I let God carry me, or do I carry my idols?
“Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29). What sin do I want him to take away during this fast?
pm.resp: Lord, carry us and save us.
interc: For the Church, that she may point all peoples to the Lamb of God.
For pastors and all who carry the burdens of others.
For a fruitful Three Days' Fast in our families and parishes.
For the unity of Christians.
For the elderly and the sick, that they may know God carries them.
pm.close: Father, you carried your people from the womb and gave us the Lamb who takes away our sins. Keep us from hardening our hearts, and bring us into your rest. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God's power is not limited, but his gifts must be received with thanks, not craving.
At Cana Mary says: do whatever he tells you, and the water becomes wine.
Christ, priest forever, always lives to intercede for us.
2027-01-24.action: Name one need of your family in prayer today, as Mary did: they have no wine.
2027-01-24.question: What has run out in my life, and have I told Jesus?
catechism: Cana and the goodness of marriage.
kidsaint: Philip told him about Jesus, and Nathanael doubted. Philip said: come and see! Nathanael met Jesus and believed. An old tradition says he later carried the Gospel to India. Lesson: invite your friends to come and see Jesus!
term: John's word for Jesus' miracles: deeds that point beyond themselves and reveal who he is. Cana is the first of his signs.

family.explain: At a wedding the wine ran out. Mary told Jesus, and then told the servants: do whatever he tells you. Jesus turned six big jars of water into the best wine! He showed everyone his glory.
family.intention: We pray for married couples and for families who are in need.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we tell Jesus about our family today?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in Kottayam kept a small notebook beside her rosary. In it she wrote the needs of her neighbours: a son without work, a couple without children, a house without peace. Each evening she told Our Lady: they have no wine. When she died, her family found forty years of names in the notebook, and beside many of them a small tick.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you revealed your glory at Cana. Fill what is empty in us as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: They have no wine (John 2:3). What has run out in my life?
Do whatever he tells you (John 2:5). What is Jesus telling me to do?
You have kept the good wine until now (John 2:10). Do I believe the best is still to come?
pm.resp: Lord, fill our jars.
interc: For the Church, that she may always point to Christ as Mary did.
For married couples, especially those in difficulty.
For families who lack food, work or peace.
For priests, who share in the priesthood of Christ.
For our group, that we may do whatever he tells us.
pm.close: Father, your Son revealed his glory and his disciples believed. Increase our faith and fill us with the joy of his presence. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God gives a prophet like Moses; we do not need diviners.
God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, lifted up for our healing.
The light has come; those who do what is true come to the light.
2027-01-31.action: Spend five minutes in silence before a crucifix today.
2027-01-31.question: Is there any darkness I am keeping away from the light?
catechism: Christ came to save, not to condemn.
kidsaint: He was a priest in Turin who loved poor boys who had no home. He gave them school, games, work and Jesus. Lesson: we can help other children come close to Jesus!
2027-01-31.special: Fifth Sunday of Denha. St John Bosco.
term: John's word for Jesus being raised on the Cross and, through the Cross, raised in glory.

family.explain: Long ago, when people were bitten by snakes, God told Moses to lift up a bronze snake on a pole, and whoever looked at it got well. Jesus was lifted up on the Cross so that everyone who looks to him with faith can live for ever. God loves the world that much!
family.intention: We pray for children and young people, through St John Bosco.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we put a crucifix where our family will see it every day?”

illus: An illustration

A family in Changanassery used to fix every journey and function by the almanac's auspicious hours. When their son's wedding date was set, the grandfather said: this time, let us ask only for God's blessing. They prayed together before the crucifix and kept the date the parish could give. The son later said it was the first time he understood that God is not a lucky charm but a Father who leads us.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, lifted up for our salvation, draw us into your light as we gather. Amen.
share: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me (Deuteronomy 18:15). Do I listen to Jesus, or to other voices about my future?
So must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). Do I look at the Cross with faith?
Those who do what is true come to the light (John 3:21). What do I need to bring into the light?
pm.resp: Lord, lead us into your light.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's love for the world.
For those trapped in superstition and fear.
For those who live in darkness and sin.
For young people, through St John Bosco.
For our group, that we may come to the light.
pm.close: Father, you so loved the world that you gave your only Son. Draw us to him lifted up, and lead us in the way we should go. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Only the Spirit of God knows the depths of God, and he teaches us to discern.
Jesus asks us to keep our lamps lit and wait for him.
The Master who comes will himself serve his faithful servants.
2027-01-02.action: Make a short examination of conscience tonight and every night this week.
2027-01-02.question: Would the Lord find me awake if he knocked today?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about servants who waited at night with their lamps lit for their master. When he came back and found them awake, he was so happy that he made them sit down and served them dinner himself!
family.intention: We pray that our family may always be ready to welcome Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we keep our lamp burning for Jesus every day?”

illus: An illustration

A night watchman at a Kochi warehouse once explained his work to a young priest: the hardest hour is not midnight but just before dawn, when nothing has happened for hours and the eyes grow heavy. He stayed awake by walking his rounds with a short prayer for each door he checked. The priest said later that he had never heard a better sermon on Luke 12.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, you search the depths of God. Open our hearts to the word of Jesus and keep our lamps burning. Amen.
share: No one comprehends what is truly God's except the Spirit of God (1 Corinthians 2:11). How do I let the Spirit teach me?
Be dressed for action and have your lamps lit (Luke 12:35). What keeps my lamp burning, and what lets it go out?
The master will come and serve them (Luke 12:37). How has Jesus served me this past year?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, keep us watchful.
interc: For the Church, that she may read the signs of the times by the light of the Spirit.
For those making important decisions at the start of this year.
For those who keep watch at night: nurses, guards, parents of sick children.
For those who have grown spiritually sleepy.
For our group, that we may be found awake when the Lord comes.
pm.close: Father, you have given us your Spirit so that we may understand your gifts. Keep us watchful and ready, and seat us at the table of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God.
The Son does what the Father does and deserves the same honour.
Our faith is the victory that conquers the world.
2027-01-04.action: Face one fear today with an act of faith.
2027-01-04.question: Do I honour Jesus as I honour the Father?

family.explain: Jesus said: I do what I see my Father doing, because the Father loves me. Jesus and the Father always work together.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always work together in love.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing do we learn by watching our parents?”

illus: An illustration

A young carpenter in Ernakulam learned his trade by watching his father for years. Customers said they could not tell which chair was made by the father and which by the son. Jesus says the same about himself and the Father: whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of the Father, you give life to whom you will. Give us your life as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God (1 John 5:1). What does being born of God mean for me?
The Son does what he sees the Father doing (John 5:19). What do I see God doing in my life?
Faith conquers the world (1 John 5:4). Where do I need faith to win?
pm.resp: Lord, increase our faith.
interc: For the Church, that she may honour the Son as she honours the Father.
For those whose faith is weak or tested.
For fathers, that their children may learn from their example.
For those who feel defeated by the world.
For our group, that our faith may become victory.
pm.close: Father, your Son does your works and gives life. Make us your children by faith, and let our faith overcome the world. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Those who believe must devote themselves to good works.
Quarrels and empty controversies are unprofitable and worthless.
Strive to enter through the narrow door; the kingdom is open to all nations.
2027-01-05.action: Light a lamp at home tonight and do one good work before you sleep.
2027-01-05.question: Do I spend more energy on arguments than on good works?

family.explain: Jesus said: try hard to go in through the narrow door. People will come from everywhere, east and west, north and south, to eat at God's great feast. Tomorrow we celebrate Jesus' Baptism, which opens that door for us.
family.intention: We pray that our family may do good works together.
family.ask: Ask: “What good work can we do together this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Pala, an old man still plants a plantain stem in his courtyard each Denha eve and sets small lamps on it. His grandchildren, home from Bengaluru and Dubai, gather round as he calls out “El Paiya!” He says: I cannot preach, but I can light a lamp and tell them who the Light is.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this eve of your manifestation, open our hearts to your word and lead us through the narrow door. Amen.
share: Those who believe in God must be careful to devote themselves to good works (Titus 3:8). What good work is God asking of me now?
Avoid controversies and quarrels (Titus 3:9). Which argument should I let go of?
Strive to enter through the narrow door (Luke 13:24). What makes the door narrow for me?
pm.resp: Christ our light, lead us in.
interc: For the Church, that she may be known by her good works.
For families keeping the Denha eve, that their lamps may be signs of faith.
For communities divided by quarrels, that they may find peace.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism.
For our group, that we may strive to enter the kingdom together.
pm.close: Father, tomorrow your Son is revealed at the Jordan. Make us zealous for good works, free us from useless quarrels, and bring us from east and west to the table of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God's wisdom is hidden from the proud and revealed by the Spirit.
What God has prepared for those who love him is beyond imagining.
At Nain Jesus had compassion and raised the widow's son.
2027-01-07.action: Visit or call someone who is grieving this week.
2027-01-07.question: Do I let God's compassion stop me on my way?

family.explain: Jesus met a mother who was crying because her only son had died. Jesus felt sorry for her and said: do not cry. He touched the stretcher and said: young man, get up! The young man sat up, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.
family.intention: We pray for families who are sad because someone they love has died.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we comfort someone who is sad?”

illus: An illustration

A parish priest near Thodupuzha was on his way to an important meeting when he passed a small house with a crowd outside: a young father had died suddenly. He stopped, prayed with the widow and stayed for an hour. He missed the meeting. Years later the widow's son, by then a priest himself, said that hour was when he first understood who Jesus is.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you had compassion on the widow of Nain. Come among us now with your wisdom and your mercy. Amen.
share: God's wisdom, secret and hidden (1 Corinthians 2:7). Where do I look for wisdom: in the world or in God?
What God has prepared for those who love him (1 Corinthians 2:9). What do I hope for from God?
When the Lord saw her, he had compassion for her (Luke 7:13). Whose tears do I see?
pm.resp: Lord, have compassion on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the wisdom of the Cross.
For widows and for mothers who have lost children.
For the dying and the dead, that they may rise with Christ.
For those who seek wisdom in the wrong places.
For our group, that we may share Christ's compassion.
pm.close: Father, your wisdom was hidden from the rulers of this age and revealed in your Son. Fill us with his compassion, and raise us with him to eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: John was the voice that prepared the way of the Lord.
He died for telling Herod the truth.
Herod's power faded; the word of God stands forever.
2027-01-08.action: Correct one wrong gently and honestly today.
2027-01-08.question: Do I stay silent when I should speak the truth with love?

family.explain: John the Baptist told King Herod that he was doing wrong. Herod put John in prison, even though he knew that John was a good and holy man. John was brave because he loved God and the truth.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard to tell the truth? How can we be brave?”

illus: An illustration

Some years ago a young Syro-Malabar priest in a North Indian mission spoke out against a landlord who was cheating poor tribal labourers. He received threats and was transferred for his safety. Years later the labourers' children, now educated, invited him back as chief guest. They said: you were our John the Baptist.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, John the Baptist prepared your way and bore witness to the truth even to death. Give us his courage and his humility. Amen.
share: Prepare the way of the Lord (Isaiah 40:3). What in my life needs to be made straight for the Lord?
I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandals (Acts 13:25). Do I point to Christ or to myself?
It is not lawful for you (Mark 6:18). Where is God asking me to speak a hard truth with love?
pm.resp: Lord, make us brave witnesses.
interc: For the persecuted Church, especially in Asia and Africa.
For prophets in our time who speak the truth to the powerful.
For rulers, that they may listen to conscience.
For those who have been silenced, threatened or imprisoned.
For our group, that we may speak the truth with love.
pm.close: Lord God, John the Baptist gave his life for the truth. Strengthen us to witness to Christ without fear, and protect all who suffer for his name. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Righteousness comes through faith, not as a wage for our works.
Christ is a stone of stumbling for the proud and a foundation for believers.
Jesus' works show that the Father is in him and he is in the Father.
2027-01-09.action: Thank God for one gift you did nothing to deserve.
2027-01-09.question: Do I build on Christ, or do I stumble over him?

family.explain: Some people did not believe that Jesus was God's Son. Jesus said: look at what I do! My good works show that the Father is in me and I am in the Father.
family.intention: We pray for people who find it hard to believe in Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What good things has Jesus done for our family?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Kozhikode working in Pune stopped going to church in college; he said he could not believe that a man could be God. A Hindu colleague invited him to help at a home run by sisters for abandoned elderly people. He went for his colleague's sake and kept going for two years. He said later: I came back to the Creed through the works, just as Jesus says in John 10.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, the Father is in you and you are in the Father. Help us to believe your works and to build our lives on you. Amen.
share: Gentiles attained righteousness through faith (Romans 9:30). Do I try to earn God's love?
Whoever believes in him will not be put to shame (Romans 9:33). Where am I afraid of being put to shame?
Believe the works (John 10:38). What works of God have I seen?
pm.resp: Lord, we believe; help our unbelief.
interc: For the Church, that her works may show the Father's love.
For those who find it hard to believe that Jesus is God.
For our Jewish brothers and sisters, the people of the first covenant.
For those who try to save themselves by their own strength.
For our group, that our faith may rest on Christ the cornerstone.
pm.close: Father, you sanctified your Son and sent him into the world. Give us faith to receive him, and let our lives rest on him who is in you, as you are in him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus prays that all who believe may be one.
Our unity flows from the communion of the Father and the Son.
Division at the Lord's table contradicts the Body of Christ.
2027-01-11.action: Take one step today towards someone you are divided from.
2027-01-11.question: Is there someone I despise or avoid, while we come to the same altar?

family.explain: Before he died, Jesus prayed for us! He asked the Father that all who believe in him would be one family, so that the world would believe.
family.intention: We pray that our family may be united and peaceful.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we need to make peace with?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Pala two families had not spoken for years because of a boundary wall. During the parish retreat the older man crossed the church after Holy Qurbana and offered his hand to his neighbour. The next week the wall was still there, but a small gate had been cut into it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you prayed that we may all be one. Gather us in your love and heal what divides us. Amen.
share: When you come together as a church, there are divisions among you (1 Corinthians 11:18). Where do I contribute to division?
That they may all be one (John 17:21). How can I serve unity in my family and parish?
So that the world may know that you have sent me (John 17:23). Does my life make Jesus believable?
pm.resp: Lord, make us one.
interc: For the unity of all Christians.
For our Syro-Malabar Church, that she may be one in faith and love around her shepherds.
For families divided by quarrels over property or pride.
For the poor who are humiliated or forgotten in our communities.
For our group, that we may be one as the Father and the Son are one.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed that we may be one in you. Heal our divisions and make us a sign of your love, so that the world may believe. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: We are one body in Christ, and every member is needed.
Jesus is the vine; apart from him we can do nothing.
We abide in his love by keeping his word.
2027-01-12.action: Thank one person whose service in the parish goes unnoticed.
2027-01-12.question: Am I staying close to the vine, or trying to bear fruit on my own?

family.explain: Jesus said he is like a vine and we are its branches. A branch stays green when it is joined to the vine. We stay alive in God when we stay close to Jesus.
family.intention: We pray that every member of our family may stay close to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we stay close to Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

A pepper farmer in Wayanad showed a group of visiting students a vine climbing a silver oak. He cut one small branch and laid it on the ground. By evening its leaves had curled. He said: the branch did nothing wrong; it was only separated. That is what happens to us without Christ.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true vine, keep us joined to you and to one another as we gather. Amen.
share: The body does not consist of one member but of many (1 Corinthians 12:14). Do I value the gifts of others?
Apart from me you can do nothing (John 15:5). Where am I trying to manage without Jesus?
Abide in my love (John 15:9). What helps me to stay in his love?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your love.
interc: For the Church, the Body of Christ, that every member may be valued.
For those who feel useless or unwanted in the community.
For those cut off from the Church, that they may be joined to the vine again.
For those going through times of pruning and trial.
For our group, that we may bear much fruit.
pm.close: Father, vinegrower of our souls, keep us joined to your Son, prune us in love and let us bear fruit that lasts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Once far off, we have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
Christ is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall.
Love for Christ comes before caring for his flock.
2027-01-13.action: Welcome someone new or alone at church this week.
2027-01-13.question: Whom do I still keep on the other side of a wall?

family.explain: St Paul says that in Jesus nobody is a stranger: we are all members of God's family.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel lonely or left out.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we welcome into our home or our circle this week?”

illus: An illustration

A family from Bihar moved to a small town in Thrissur district for work. At their first Sunday Qurbana they stood at the back, unsure of the language. An elderly woman walked over, took the children by the hand and seated them beside her grandchildren. Years later the father said: that day we stopped being migrants and became parishioners.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are our peace. Break down every wall among us and make us one household as we gather. Amen.
share: You who once were far off have been brought near (Ephesians 2:13). How has God brought me near?
He has broken down the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:14). What walls remain in my heart?
Do you love me? Feed my sheep (John 21:17). Whom has the Lord entrusted to my care?
pm.resp: Lord, you are our peace.
interc: For the Pope, our Major Archbishop and all pastors, that they may feed Christ's flock with love.
For migrants and strangers, that they may find a home in the Church.
For communities divided by caste, language or region.
For parents and catechists who feed the young in faith.
For our group, that we may welcome others as we have been welcomed.
pm.close: Father, through the Cross of your Son you have made us one household. Keep us in his peace and make us faithful in caring for his sheep. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus commands the storm: Peace! Be still!
Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.
St Devasahayam stayed steadfast in faith to the end.
2027-01-14.action: Hand over your heaviest worry to Jesus today.
2027-01-14.question: In my storms, do I believe that Jesus cares?

family.explain: A big storm came while Jesus was asleep in the boat. The disciples were scared. Jesus woke up and said to the sea: Peace! Be still! And everything became calm.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who is afraid today, and for Christians who suffer for Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes you afraid? Shall we tell Jesus about it?”

illus: An illustration

St Devasahayam was born Neelakanta Pillai near Nagercoil. After his Baptism he took the name Lazarus, Devasahayam in Tamil and Malayalam, meaning “God is my help”. Arrested in 1749, he was paraded through towns and kept in chains for nearly three years, praying and encouraging those who came to him. He was shot dead at Aralvaimozhy in 1752, and was canonised in 2022.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Lord of wind and sea, calm our hearts as we gather, and make us steadfast in faith like St Devasahayam. Amen.
share: Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing? (Mark 4:38). When have I prayed like this?
Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you (1 Peter 5:7). What anxiety do I need to hand over?
Resist him, steadfast in your faith (1 Peter 5:9). Where is my faith being tested?
pm.resp: Lord, calm our storms.
interc: For the Church, that she may trust Christ in every storm.
For those overwhelmed by anxiety and fear.
For the Church in India, through the prayers of St Devasahayam.
For Christians who suffer for their faith.
For our group, that we may stay steadfast in faith.
pm.close: Father, your Son commands the wind and the sea, and you care for us. Through the prayers of St Devasahayam make us steadfast in faith and free from fear. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter confesses Jesus as the Messiah, the Son of the living God.
On this rock Christ builds his Church and gives Peter the keys.
Peter raises Tabitha; Paul boasts only of his weakness.
2027-01-15.action: Pray today for the Pope and our Major Archbishop.
2027-01-15.question: Who do I say that Jesus is, not only in words but in my life?

family.explain: Jesus asked his friends: who do you say that I am? Peter said: you are the Christ, the Son of the living God! Jesus called him the rock on which he would build his Church.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and for our bishops and priests.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is Jesus for you?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Changanacherry a group of widows meets every Thursday to sew uniforms for poor schoolchildren. They call themselves the Tabitha group. One of them said: we cannot preach like Peter or travel like Paul, but we can sew, and every stitch is a prayer for a child.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of the living God, you ask us: who do you say that I am? Help us to answer with our lips and with our lives. Amen.
share: But who do you say that I am? (Matthew 16:15). What is my own answer?
Tabitha, get up (Acts 9:40). Where does Jesus want to raise up life through me?
If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness (2 Corinthians 11:30). How has God worked through my weakness?
pm.resp: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
interc: For the Pope, the Successor of Peter.
For our Major Archbishop and bishops.
For missionaries who suffer for the Gospel.
For widows, and for all who serve the poor with their hands.
For our group, that we may confess Christ without fear.
pm.close: Father, you revealed your Son to Peter and sent Paul to the nations. Keep us in the faith of the apostles and make us bearers of life to others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus teaches with authority, and evil obeys him.
We believe with the heart and confess with the mouth.
Faith comes from what is heard, so someone must be sent.
2027-01-16.action: Speak gently about your faith to one person this week.
2027-01-16.question: Has anyone ever heard about Jesus from my mouth?

family.explain: St Paul says that people can believe in Jesus only if someone tells them about him. The feet of those who bring the good news are beautiful!
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and for those who have never heard of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Who told you about Jesus, and whom could we tell?”

illus: An illustration

An old catechist in Idukki taught Sunday school for forty years. At his funeral the church was full of men and women who had once sat on his benches. The parish priest said: he never travelled far, but his feet were beautiful; half this parish first heard the good news from his mouth.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, speak your word with authority among us, and free us from every evil. Amen.
share: He taught them as one having authority (Mark 1:22). Do I let Jesus' word have authority over my life?
Be silent, and come out of him! (Mark 1:25). What needs to be silenced and driven out of my heart?
How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news! (Romans 10:15). Where is the Lord sending me?
pm.resp: Lord, speak, and set us free.
interc: For preachers and catechists, that they may proclaim the word with faith.
For missionaries, especially those from our Church serving far from home.
For those oppressed by evil, addiction or fear.
For those who have never heard the name of Jesus.
For our group, that our feet may carry the good news.
pm.close: Father, faith comes from what is heard. Open our ears to the word of your Son, and send us to speak it with love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: We are the clay; God is our Father and potter.
Pray for everyone; God desires all to be saved.
Forgive from the heart as you have been forgiven.
2027-01-18.action: Keep today's fast and forgive one person from your heart.
2027-01-18.question: Whom do I still hold by the throat over a small debt?

family.explain: A king forgave a servant a huge debt. But that servant would not forgive a friend who owed him a little. Jesus says: God has forgiven us so much, so we must forgive others.
family.intention: We pray for our country, our leaders and the whole world, as St Paul asks.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family we need to forgive today?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers near Pala had not spoken for nine years over a strip of rubber land. On the first morning of Moonnu Nombu the younger one heard the parable of the unforgiving servant at Qurbana. That evening he walked to his brother's gate with the land papers and said: keep it; I want my brother more than the land. Their mother said it was the best fast the family had ever kept.

pm.open: Merciful Father, as we begin the fast of the Ninevites, shape us like clay in your hands and teach us to forgive. Amen.
share: We are the clay, and you are our potter (Isaiah 64:8). Do I let God reshape me?
Prayers for everyone (1 Timothy 2:1). Whom do I forget to pray for?
Forgive your brother or sister from your heart (Matthew 18:35). Whom must I forgive?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that these three days may bring true conversion.
For rulers and all in authority, as St Paul asks.
For those who carry grudges and those who cannot forgive.
For the unity of Christians.
For our group, that our fasting may make us merciful.
pm.close: Lord God, you are our Father and we are the work of your hand. Forgive us as we forgive, and renew us through prayer and fasting. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Return to God with all your heart and put away idols.
Our sins are the barrier, not God's weakness.
The humble tax collector, not the proud Pharisee, goes home justified.
2027-01-19.action: Repeat the tax collector's prayer throughout the day.
2027-01-19.question: Does my fasting make me humbler, or does it make me compare myself with others?

family.explain: Two men went to pray. One said: God, I am better than others! The other said: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. Jesus said the second man pleased God.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel far from God, and for ourselves, that we may be humble.
family.ask: Ask: “Let us all say together slowly: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.”

illus: An illustration

A church trustee in Thrissur had kept every fast for forty years and told everyone so. During one Moonnu Nombu his grandson asked him why he always sat in the front pew while old Kunjamma sat near the door. The question stayed with him. The next day he sat at the back beside her, and found that for the first time he prayed: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.

pm.open: Lord God, your hand is not too short to save. Remove the barriers between us and you, and make us humble. Amen.
share: If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, put away the foreign gods (1 Samuel 7:3). What idol must I put away?
Your iniquities have been barriers between you and your God (Isaiah 59:2). What stands between me and God?
God, be merciful to me, a sinner! (Luke 18:13). Do I pray like the Pharisee or like the tax collector?
pm.resp: God, be merciful to us, sinners.
interc: For the Church, that her fasting may be humble and sincere.
For those who despise others and those who are despised.
For all who feel their prayers are unheard.
For the unity of Christians, one body in Christ.
For our group, that we may be transformed by the renewing of our minds.
pm.close: Father, you lift up the humble. Accept our fast and our prayer, take away our sins, and make us one body in Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Nineveh believed God, fasted and turned; God relented.
God gathers objects of mercy from every people.
Give and pray in secret; your Father sees.
2027-01-20.action: Give what you saved by fasting to someone in need, without telling anyone.
2027-01-20.question: Is my fasting for God's eyes or for the eyes of others?

family.explain: Jonah told the people of Nineveh that God was angry with their sins. Everyone, even the king and the children, said sorry and fasted. God saw them change and forgave them.
family.intention: We pray for our bishops named Sebastian and for soldiers and police.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we help someone in secret this week, so that only God knows?”

illus: An illustration

On the third day of Moonnu Nombu at Kuravilangad, men carry a large model ship around the church, remembering Jonah. An old pilgrim was asked why he came every year. He said: not to see the ship. I bring my sins and leave them with God, as Nineveh did. And on the way home I give my fast-money to the first beggar I meet, without telling my wife, so that only God knows.

pm.open: Merciful God, as our fast ends, spare your people and teach us to do good in secret. Amen.
share: Sanctify a fast; gather the children (Joel 2:15–16). Does my whole family share in the fast?
Who knows? God may relent (Jonah 3:9). Do I believe God's mercy can change what seems fixed?
Your Father who sees in secret will reward you (Matthew 6:4). What good can I do where no one sees?
pm.resp: Spare your people, O Lord.
interc: For the fruits of the Three Days' Fast in our Church.
For Mar Sebastian Vadakkel, Mar Sebastian Adayanthrath, Mar Sebastian Vaniyapurackal and Mar Sebastian Pozholiparampil.
For soldiers and police, through St Sebastian.
For cities and nations in danger, that they may turn to God.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, you spared Nineveh when it repented. Spare us, make us objects of your mercy, and reward in secret what we do for love of you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God has no pleasure in the death of the wicked.
He casts our sins into the depths of the sea.
Heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents.
2027-01-21.action: Contact one person who has drifted from the Church.
2027-01-21.question: Do I share God's joy when a sinner returns, or do I grumble?

family.explain: A shepherd lost one sheep. He looked everywhere until he found it, then carried it home happily. God is that happy when someone comes back to him!
family.intention: We pray for people who are lost and far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “How did the fast help our family?”

illus: An illustration

In Kerala fishing villages, when a boat lost at sea for days finally returns, the whole beach runs to meet it, church bells ring and there is a feast. A fisherman said: that is how heaven is when one of us comes back to God.

pm.open: God of mercy, the fast is over and your mercy remains. Fill us with your joy over every sinner who returns. Amen.
share: I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked (Ezekiel 33:11). Do I believe God wants me to live?
You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea (Micah 7:19). What sin do I need to leave there?
Rejoice with me (Luke 15:6). Do I rejoice when others return to God?
pm.resp: Lord, we rejoice in your mercy.
interc: In thanksgiving for the graces of the Three Days' Fast.
For those still far from God.
For priests who seek the lost.
For families waiting for a member to return.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, you delight in showing mercy. Keep us in the joy of your forgiveness and make us seekers of the lost. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: On Carmel God showed that he alone is God.
Jesus sends the Twelve to proclaim the kingdom.
Through the Gospel the Evangelists became our fathers in faith.
2027-01-22.action: Begin reading one Gospel, a chapter a day.
2027-01-22.question: To whom can I be a father or mother in faith?

family.explain: Jesus chose twelve friends and sent them to tell everyone that God's kingdom is near. Matthew and John were among them, and later they wrote down the Good News for us. Mark and Luke wrote Gospels too.
family.intention: We pray that all people may hear the Gospel.
family.ask: Ask: “Do you know the names of the four Gospel writers?”

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in Idukki has given away more than five hundred copies of the Gospel of Luke in Malayalam, one at a time, to bus conductors, nurses and neighbours. Asked why, she said: someone gave me the Gospel for nothing when I was a girl. I received without payment; I give without payment.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, through your apostles and Evangelists your word has reached us. Open our hearts as we gather to hear it. Amen.
share: The LORD indeed is God (1 Kings 18:39). Where do I need God to show himself in my life?
Proclaim the good news (Matthew 10:7). With whom can I share the Gospel this week?
I became your father through the gospel (1 Corinthians 4:15). Who brought the Gospel to me?
pm.resp: Lord, you alone are God.
interc: For preachers and teachers of the Gospel.
For Bible translators and those who spread Scripture.
For those who have never heard the Gospel.
For Christian unity around the word of God.
For our group, that we may give freely what we have received.
pm.close: Father, through the Evangelists you gave us the Gospel of your Son. Send us out to proclaim it with joy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Live in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ.
Christians are called to strive side by side, with one mind.
The Canaanite woman's humble, persistent faith is praised by Jesus.
2027-01-23.action: Bring one intention to Jesus every day this week: Lord, help me.
2027-01-23.question: Do I give up on prayer when God seems silent?

family.explain: A mother from another country begged Jesus to heal her daughter. Even when it seemed Jesus said no, she kept asking. Jesus said: woman, great is your faith! And her daughter was healed.
family.intention: We pray for Christians of all Churches, that we may be one.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we will keep asking Jesus for, every day, as a family?”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Kannur prayed every evening for twelve years for her son, who was lost in drink. Relatives told her to stop wasting her breath. She answered: even the dogs eat the crumbs; I am only asking for a crumb. One Easter her son walked into the parish church and asked for confession. She says she still prays the same prayer, now for other mothers.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. Give us a faith that does not give up. Amen.
share: Live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ (Philippians 1:27). Where does my life not match my faith?
Lord, help me (Matthew 15:25). What do I need to keep asking for?
Woman, great is your faith! (Matthew 15:28). Would Jesus say this of my faith?
pm.resp: Lord, help us.
interc: For all Christians, that we may strive side by side for the Gospel.
For parents praying for their children.
For those who feel God is silent.
For Christians who suffer for their faith.
For our group, that our faith may be humble and persistent.
pm.close: Father, you hear the cry of every nation. Grant us the faith of the Canaanite woman and the unity Paul prayed for. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God called Moses and Saul by name.
Paul: by the grace of God I am what I am.
The latecomers in the vineyard receive the same generous wage.
2027-01-25.action: Rejoice sincerely in someone else's blessing today.
2027-01-25.question: Do I resent God's generosity to others?
kidsaint: He was angry with Christians until Jesus spoke to him on the road. Then he became Jesus' best messenger. Lesson: God can use anyone, even someone who started badly!
2027-01-25.special: Conversion of St Paul. Conclusion of the Church Unity Octave.
term: God's gift of his own life and help, given without our earning it.

family.explain: A farm owner paid everyone the same, even those who came to work late. Some were cross. God is generous to everyone!
family.intention: We pray for Christians of all Churches, that they may be one.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be happy when good things happen to others?”

illus: An illustration

A man from Changanassery was baptized at sixty-eight after years of mocking his wife's faith. At his first Communion he wept and said: I came at the eleventh hour, and the Lord gave me the full wage. His wife said: I prayed forty years; it was worth every day.

pm.open: Lord, you call us by name and give us grace we do not earn. Make us grateful and generous. Amen.
share: Moses, Moses! (Exodus 3:4). Do I hear God calling me by name?
Who are you, Lord? (Acts 9:5). Do I know Jesus personally?
Are you envious because I am generous? (Matthew 20:15). Where am I envious?
pm.resp: Lord, by your grace we are what we are.
interc: For the unity of Christians, at the end of the Unity Octave.
For those who persecute the Church.
For late converts and those returning to faith.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism.
For our group, that we may rejoice in one another's gifts.
pm.close: Father, your grace is generous to all. Free us from envy and make us witnesses of your mercy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God's rest is still open; today, do not harden your hearts.
At Nazareth familiarity turned to contempt.
God's mercy reaches beyond every border.
2027-01-26.action: Read today's Gospel again this evening and obey one word of it.
2027-01-26.question: Have I stopped listening to someone because I know them too well?

family.explain: Jesus went home to Nazareth. At first people liked his words, but then they said: he is only Joseph's son! They got angry and did not listen. Jesus is God's Son, and we must listen to him every day.
family.intention: We pray for India on Republic Day, and for people of all religions who live together.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family we need to listen to better?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Kanjirappally a young engineer came home to start a waste-recycling unit. The elders laughed: we knew him when he ran barefoot in the paddy fields. Only when the district collector praised the project did they listen. At the Republic Day assembly the parish priest read Luke 4 and said: sometimes God's gift is the person we think we know too well.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, today we want to hear your voice. Soften our hearts and bless our nation. Amen.
share: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 4:7). Where is my heart hard?
Is not this Joseph's son? (Luke 4:22). Whom do I despise because I know them too well?
He passed through the midst of them and went on his way (Luke 4:30). Do I let Jesus go on his way without me?
pm.resp: Lord, soften our hearts.
interc: For India on Republic Day: for justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
For the President, the Prime Minister and all who govern.
For religious freedom and harmony among communities.
For bishops, through Sts Timothy and Titus.
For our group, that we may hear God's voice today.
pm.close: Father, your Son was rejected in his own town and still offered salvation to all. Make us listen to him and serve our nation in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: There is no other gospel than the Gospel of Christ.
A servant of Christ seeks God's approval, not people's.
The sheep know the Shepherd's voice; he calls them by name.
2027-01-27.action: Read one chapter of a Gospel slowly today.
2027-01-27.question: Whose approval do I seek most?

family.explain: A good shepherd knows the name of every sheep, and the sheep know his voice. Jesus is our Shepherd. He knows your name, and he wants you to know his voice.
family.intention: We pray for those who are confused by false teaching.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we learn to recognise Jesus' voice?”

illus: An illustration

A shepherd in the hills near Vagamon was asked how his flock never mixed with his neighbour's when both grazed together. He smiled, called once, and his goats lifted their heads and came. They know my voice, he said. I have talked to them every day since they were born.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, good Shepherd, call us by name and lead us. Amen.
share: Turning to a different gospel (Galatians 1:6). Where am I tempted by a gospel without the Cross?
Am I trying to please people? (Galatians 1:10). Whose approval do I seek?
The sheep follow him because they know his voice (John 10:4). How do I recognise his voice?
pm.resp: Lord, we listen for your voice.
interc: For the Church, that she may guard the one Gospel.
For preachers and teachers, that they may seek God's approval.
For those confused by false teaching.
For those who have strayed from the flock.
For our group, that we may know the Shepherd's voice.
