pm.close: Father, your Son calls us by name. Keep us in the truth of his Gospel and lead us after him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The love of Christ urges us on: one has died for all.
Jesus asks: What are you looking for? Come and see.
St Thomas Aquinas wanted nothing but the Lord.
2027-01-28.action: Write one sentence in answer to Jesus' question: What are you looking for?
2027-01-28.question: What am I really looking for in life?

family.explain: Two friends followed Jesus. He turned and asked: What are you looking for? He said: come and see! They stayed with him all day. Then Andrew ran to tell his brother Simon: we have found the Messiah!
family.intention: We pray for students and teachers, through St Thomas Aquinas.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we invite to come and see Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A college student in Thrissur, preparing for exams, pasted a small card above her desk with a prayer of St Thomas Aquinas for study. Her room-mate, who never went to church, asked what it meant. The answer led to a long conversation, and a few months later the room-mate came with her to the Sunday Qurbana. Come and see, the student said later, is still the best invitation.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Lamb of God, we come to see where you are staying. Let us remain with you. Amen.
share: The love of Christ urges us on (2 Corinthians 5:14). What urges me on?
What are you looking for? (John 1:38). How do I answer Jesus?
We have found the Messiah (John 1:41). Whom can I bring to Jesus?
pm.resp: Lord, we want to remain with you.
interc: For all who are searching for God.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life.
For theologians, teachers and students, through St Thomas Aquinas.
For our families, that we may bring one another to Christ.
For our group, that the love of Christ may urge us on.
pm.close: Father, your Son invites us to come and see. Draw us to remain with him and to bring others to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Naboth was falsely accused and stoned for keeping his inheritance.
Stephen saw heaven opened and forgave as he died.
Afflicted but not crushed: the life of Jesus shows in our weakness.
2027-01-29.action: Pray by name for one country where Christians are persecuted.
2027-01-29.question: When I am struck down, do I look at what can be seen or at what cannot be seen?

family.explain: Stephen loved Jesus so much that, even when people threw stones at him, he looked up and saw Jesus in heaven. He forgave them, just like Jesus did.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith today.
family.ask: Ask: “When someone hurts us, can we pray for them like Stephen?”

illus: An illustration

After the violence against Christians in Kandhamal, Odisha, in 2008, many families who had lost homes and loved ones came back to rebuild their villages and their chapels. Visitors who met them were often struck by one thing: how many spoke of forgiving those who had attacked them. Afflicted, but not crushed; struck down, but not destroyed.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, give us the faith of St Stephen, to see heaven opened even in suffering. Amen.
share: I will not give you my ancestral inheritance (1 Kings 21:3). What part of my faith am I tempted to sell?
I see the heavens opened (Acts 7:56). Where do I look when I suffer?
Afflicted in every way, but not crushed (2 Corinthians 4:8). What affliction can I offer today?
pm.resp: Lord Jesus, receive our spirit.
interc: For persecuted Christians throughout the world.
For the falsely accused and those who lose their land and homes to the powerful.
For persecutors, that they may be converted like Saul.
For deacons, following St Stephen.
For our group, that we may forgive.
pm.close: Father, your Son gathered his people like a hen gathers her brood. Through St Stephen, keep us faithful and forgiving. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: We can know that we have eternal life and pray with confidence.
Pray for those who sin, so that God may give them life.
Whoever is from God hears the words of God.
2027-01-30.action: Pray by name for someone who has fallen into sin, instead of talking about them.
2027-01-30.question: Whose child do I resemble in the way I speak and act?

family.explain: Jesus said that if God is our Father, we will love Jesus and listen to his words. Children often look like their parents. God's children look like Jesus when they listen to him and tell the truth.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family or parish who has turned away from God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a small lie we need to say sorry for today?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Ernakulam a prayer group kept a simple rule: whenever someone mentioned another person's fault, the group stopped and prayed for that person before saying anything more. The leader said: John tells us to pray for a brother who sins, not to discuss him. The gossip stopped, and two people who had left the parish came back that year.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the true God and eternal life. Keep us in your truth. Amen.
share: If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us (1 John 5:14). Do I pray with confidence?
Little children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). What idol do I need to put away?
Whoever is from God hears the words of God (John 8:47). How do I listen to God?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your truth.
interc: For sinners, that God may give them life.
For those enslaved by lies and deception.
For priests who hear confessions.
For people searching for the true God.
For our group, that we may pray for one another instead of judging.
pm.close: Father, you have given us your Son, the true God and eternal life. Make us your children in truth and love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed new year to you all. On this first day of the year the Church does not begin with our plans but with a Name: the Holy Name of Jesus. Eight days after his birth, the Child was circumcised and named Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived (Luke 2:21).

In the Bible a name is never only a label. In the first reading God changes Abram's name to Abraham, father of a multitude, and gives him the covenant (Genesis 17:5). And through Isaiah he says to his people: I have called you by name, you are mine (Isaiah 43:1). Each of us was called by name at Baptism. God knows you, not as a number, but by name.

The name Jesus means the Lord saves. The angel says to Joseph: you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21). We may want many things from the new year: health, a job, success for our children. Jesus comes first to save us from sin, the root of every other sorrow.

St Paul tells us how this Name was won. Christ Jesus emptied himself, took the form of a slave, humbled himself and became obedient to death on a cross. Therefore God highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name (Philippians 2:7–9). The way to glory is the way of humility.

Today is also the last Friday of Nativity, when our Church honours the Divine Motherhood of Mary. She who gave Jesus his human flesh is truly the Mother of God, and she stands with the Apostles in prayer (Acts 1:14). Let us begin this year with her.

So let us make a simple resolution: to call on the Name of Jesus every day. Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner. Let this Name be on our lips in joy and in trouble, and this year will be blessed. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Jesus' name day! The name Jesus means God saves us. Let us say his name with love every day.
Do you know your own name's meaning? Ask your parents tonight, and thank God for calling you by name.

intro: On the eighth day the Child received the name Jesus, which means “the Lord saves”. We begin the year by calling on that name.

sub: The angel chose it before his birth (Matthew 1:21).
His name tells us his mission.
points.apply: Learn the meaning of your own baptismal name.

sub: He humbled himself to the cross.
points.apply: Bow your head whenever the name of Jesus is spoken at the Holy Qurbana.

sub: A year lived in his name.
points.apply: Begin each day this year with the name of Jesus.

concl: The name of Jesus is our programme for the new year: God saves.
Whatever this year holds, we face it in his name.
opts.resolve: This year I will begin and end each day by calling on the name of Jesus.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed new year to all of you. On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised and was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived (Luke 2:21). The name means the Lord saves. God chose it himself.

In the Bible a name is a mission. The angel told Joseph: you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21). Every time we say the name of Jesus, we confess what he came to do.

Paul tells us that because Jesus humbled himself to the cross, God gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend (Philippians 2:9–10). That is why we bow our heads at his name.

Peter, standing before the council, said: there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). We do not know what this year will bring. But we know the name in which we will face it.

So let us begin the year as the Church begins it: in the name of Jesus. Let it be the first word on our lips in the morning and the last at night. And may the Lord bless us and keep us in his name throughout this year. Amen.

opts.a: Mary, Mother of God, and the year ahead
intro: In 431 the Council of Ephesus proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God. The first day of the year belongs to her and to her Son.

sub: Not mother of a man only.
The Son she bore is God.
Ephesus defended Christ by honouring Mary.
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly today, weighing the words “Mother of God”.

sub: Mary keeps it in her heart.
A heart that remembers God's deeds.
points.apply: Each night this year, recall one thing God did that day.

sub: So that we might be children.
points.apply: Put your family under Mary's protection for the year.

concl: Mary, Mother of God, is also our mother.
With her we begin the year pondering God's works in our hearts.
opts.resolve: I will entrust this year to Mary, Mother of God, and keep a habit of thanksgiving each night.
homily: Dear friends, today the Church greets Mary with her greatest title: Mother of God. In the year 431 the bishops gathered at Ephesus defended this title, because the Child she bore is not a man who later became God, but the eternal Son of God made man. Honouring Mary protects the truth about Jesus.
Paul says: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). God did not come among us from nowhere. He came through a mother, through a family, through a people.

When the shepherds told what they had seen, Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). She did not understand everything, but she kept it and turned it over in prayer. That is a good way to live a year.
Paul adds: because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father (Galatians 4:6). Through Mary's Son we become children of God.

So let us begin the year with her. Let us ask Mary, Mother of God, to keep our families, and let us learn from her to ponder each day what God has done. And may the Lord bless us and keep us, and give us peace. Amen.

Dear brothers and sisters, in three days we will celebrate Denha, when the Spirit came down upon Jesus at the Jordan. Today's readings prepare us by showing God as the one who hears, comes down and sets free.

Moses is keeping sheep in the wilderness when he sees a bush that burns without being consumed. From the fire God calls him by name and says: I have observed the misery of my people; I have heard their cry; I know their sufferings, and I have come down to deliver them (Exodus 3:7–8). Our God is not deaf to the cries of his people.

Moses protests: who am I that I should go to Pharaoh? God does not tell him how gifted he is. He says only: I will be with you (Exodus 3:11–12). That promise is enough for every mission, every vocation, every difficult task.

In Isaiah God does something more surprising still. He calls Cyrus, a foreign king, his anointed, and says: I call you by your name, though you do not know me (Isaiah 45:4). God can use anyone to save his people. But Cyrus is only a shadow. In Nazareth Jesus stands up in the synagogue and reads: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. Then he says: today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing (Luke 4:18, 21). The true Anointed, the Mshiha, is here.

How does this good news reach us? St Paul reminds Timothy that from childhood he has known the sacred writings that instruct him for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 3:15). Faith comes to us through families, catechism teachers and parishes, from one generation to the next.

Today we also celebrate St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. Like Moses, he heard the cry of his people, the poor and the unlettered, and he answered by asking that a school stand beside every church. Let us ask for his spirit: to hear the cry of the poor, to trust the promise I will be with you, and to hand on the word of God to our children. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus went to the synagogue in his home town and read from the Bible: God has sent me to bring good news to the poor! Then he said: today it has come true.
St Chavara wanted every child to learn to read, so that they could know God's word. Let us read a little of the Bible with our family this week.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed feast of Denha to you. Denha means dawn, rising, manifestation. Our Church celebrates today the Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan, because there the whole mystery of God was revealed.

Look at the scene in Matthew. Jesus comes from Galilee to John at the Jordan to be baptised. John tries to stop him: I need to be baptised by you, and do you come to me? Jesus answers: let it be so now; it is proper for us in this way to fulfil all righteousness (Matthew 3:14–15). The sinless one takes his place in the line of sinners.

And when he comes up from the water, the heavens are opened, the Spirit of God descends like a dove and alights on him, and a voice from heaven says: this is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased (Matthew 3:16–17). Son, Spirit and Father: the Holy Trinity is revealed.

Long before, Balaam had seen from afar: a star shall come out of Jacob (Numbers 24:17). Isaiah had promised a shoot from the stump of Jesse on whom the spirit of the Lord would rest, the spirit of wisdom and understanding (Isaiah 11:1–2). At the Jordan the star rises and the Spirit rests. The dawn has come.

Our ancestors kept this feast beautifully. They lit lamps on plantain stems and walked around crying El Paiya, God is light. On the eve they bathed in rivers and ponds, remembering the Jordan. These customs said: we are baptised; we are children of light.

St Paul tells Titus that God saved us, not because of works we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit, poured out on us richly (Titus 3:5–6). Many of us were baptised as infants and rarely think of it. Today, let us remember: God has said to you, you are my beloved son, my beloved daughter. Let us live as people who have heard that voice. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Denha! Jesus was baptised in the river Jordan. The Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and God said: this is my beloved Son!
When you were baptised, God said the same about you: you are my beloved child. Ask your parents when your Baptism day is!

intro: Isaiah prayed: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down.” At the Jordan the prayer is answered.

points.apply: Thank God for coming close to you.
Make the sign of the cross slowly and with faith today.

sub: He sanctifies the water for us.
points.apply: Bless yourself with holy water when you enter church.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opens and the Trinity is revealed.
In Baptism heaven opened for us too.
opts.resolve: I will make the sign of the cross with faith, remembering that heaven opened at my Baptism.
homily: Dear friends, long ago Isaiah cried out: O that you would tear open the heavens and come down (Isaiah 64:1). Israel longed for God to come close. At the Jordan the prayer is answered: as Jesus came up from the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him (Mark 1:10).

This is the great manifestation of the Trinity. The Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends, and the Father's voice says: this is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased (Matthew 3:17). Every time we make the sign of the cross, we confess what was revealed at the Jordan.
Jesus did not need to be cleansed. The Fathers said: he went into the water not to be made holy by it, but to make the waters holy for us. From that day, water became the doorway into God's life.

Paul says: he saved us through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). What happened at the Jordan happened to us at the font. Heaven opened over us; the Father called us his children.
Today let us thank God for our Baptism, make the sign of the cross with faith, and come to the Holy Qurbana as children of an open heaven. Amen.

intro: Most of us were baptised as infants and remember nothing. Today the Church asks us to remember what God did.

points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and celebrate it.
Live one day this week as if wearing your baptismal garment.

sub: The candle lit from the Easter flame.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises tonight: I reject sin; I believe.

concl: Baptism is not only a past event but a present identity.
We live as children of God, clothed with Christ, walking in the light.
opts.resolve: This week I will find my Baptism date, thank my godparents, and renew my baptismal promises.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, most of us were baptised as infants. We do not remember the water, the oil or the candle. Today, as we celebrate the Lord's own baptism, the Church invites us to remember what God did to us.

Paul asks: do you not know that all of us who have been baptised into Christ Jesus were baptised into his death? We were buried with him by baptism, so that we too might walk in newness of life (Romans 6:3–4). The font is both a tomb and a womb.

He also says: as many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ (Galatians 3:27). That is why we received a white garment. We are called to wear Christ every day, at home, at work, in our words.

At Baptism a candle was lit for us, and our godparents spoke promises on our behalf: to reject sin and to believe. Now that we are grown, those promises are ours to keep. Once you were darkness, but now in the Lord you are light (Ephesians 5:8).
So let us find the date of our Baptism, thank our godparents, and tonight renew our promises: I reject sin; I believe in God. Then come to the Holy Qurbana as children of the light. Amen.

Dear brothers and sisters, the season of Denha keeps one question before us: how has God shown himself to us? Today's Gospel answers in a single line: the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory (John 1:14).

Long before Bethlehem, God was already a travelling God. In the Book of Numbers Israel leaves Sinai with the ark of the covenant going before them to seek out a resting place for them, and the cloud of the Lord over them by day (Numbers 10:33–34). Moses even begs his relative Hobab to come along: come with us, and we will treat you well. And whenever the ark set out, Moses prayed: Arise, O Lord! God did not stay on the mountain; he went ahead of his people.

Yet Isaiah also knows the pain of faith: truly, you are a God who hides himself (Isaiah 45:15). Many of us know that feeling. We pray, and God seems silent. John gives the answer: no one has ever seen God; it is God the only Son, close to the Father's heart, who has made him known (John 1:18). If you want to know what God is like, look at Jesus.

The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Moses was faithful in God's house as a servant, but Christ is faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house (Hebrews 3:5–6). John says: the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ (John 1:17). The law showed the way; Jesus is the Way himself.

From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace (John 1:16). Every Holy Qurbana is that fullness given again. The Word who pitched his tent among us comes to dwell in us, and we leave the church as his house, carrying him into our streets and homes.

So this week, before you leave home each morning, pray the prayer of Moses: Arise, O Lord, go before me today. And each night count one grace you received. We are his house; let us let him live in it. Amen.
kids: Children, long ago God's people carried a special golden box called the ark, and it went in front of them on the road to show that God was with them. Then God did something even better: his Son Jesus became a baby and came to live with us!
When you walk to school, say: Jesus, walk in front of me today. He will!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today's readings ask: who carries whom? Moses is exhausted. The people complain about food, and he cries to God: I am not able to carry all this people alone, for they are too heavy for me (Numbers 11:14). Many parents, priests and caregivers know that prayer.

God does not scold Moses. He takes some of the spirit that is on him and puts it on seventy elders, so that they shall bear the burden of the people along with you (Numbers 11:17). God's answer to our exhaustion is his Spirit, and brothers and sisters to share the load.

Isaiah gives a strong picture. In Babylon the statues of Bel and Nebo were carried through the streets on festival days. The prophet sees them loaded on weary animals, bowing and stooping: gods that have to be carried and cannot save. Then God speaks to his people: I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save (Isaiah 46:4). Idols are carried. The true God carries.

In the Gospel John the Baptist sees Jesus and cries: here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29). The heaviest burden of all, the sin of the world, no Moses could carry. The Lamb lifts it and carries it away, to the cross.

Hebrews tells us where the journey ends: a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God (Hebrews 4:9). And it warns: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts. Tomorrow we begin the Three Days' Fast. Our ancestors kept it with great devotion; many still go to Kuravilangad and other shrines.

Let us keep it in the spirit of today's readings. Put down the idols we carry. Share someone else's burden. Give our sins to the Lamb who takes them away. And let him carry us, as he promised, even when we turn gray. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist pointed to Jesus and said: here is the Lamb of God! Jesus takes away our sins.
When you are tired or sad, remember: God says, I will carry you. Tomorrow the Three Days' Fast begins. What small thing can you give up for Jesus?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in Denha Christ is revealed, and today he is revealed at a wedding. But first we hear Moses in the wilderness, wondering how so many can be fed. God answers: is the LORD's power limited? He shares his spirit with the elders, sends the quails, and yet the people grab them with greed, and the place is called the graves of craving.

Isaiah tells us the difference between idols and God. Idols must be carried on shoulders and cannot answer. The living God carries his people and says: I am God, and there is no one like me (Isaiah 46:9).
At Cana the wine runs out. Mary notices and says to her Son: they have no wine (John 2:3). Then she says to the servants the words she still says to us: do whatever he tells you (John 2:5).

The servants fill six stone jars to the brim with water, and Jesus changes it into wine, the best wine, kept until now. John says: he revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him (John 2:11).

Hebrews tells us that Christ holds his priesthood permanently and always lives to make intercession for us (Hebrews 7:25). The jars of purification are filled with something new: his own self-offering, made present at every Holy Qurbana.
So let us tell Jesus what has run out in our homes, receive his gifts with thanks and not with craving, and do whatever he tells us. The good wine is still to come. Amen.
kids: Children, at a wedding the wine ran out, and Mary told Jesus. Jesus turned water into the best wine!
When something is missing in your family, tell Jesus, and do what he says.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Moses tells Israel not to seek the future from soothsayers and diviners, but to trust God's promise: the LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet (Deuteronomy 18:15).

Through Isaiah, God says: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your own good, who leads you in the way you should go (Isaiah 48:17). God is not a power to be managed by horoscopes and lucky times. He is a Father who teaches and leads.

In the Gospel Jesus, the Prophet like Moses, tells Nicodemus: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life (John 3:14–15).

And then the heart of the Gospel: God so loved the world that he gave his only Son (John 3:16). He did not come to condemn but to save. Judgment happens when we prefer darkness; salvation, when we come to the light.
Hebrews tells us not to become sluggish, but to imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises (Hebrews 6:12), like Abraham, who waited and obtained the promise.
Let us look at the Cross, leave every superstition, and bring our deeds into the light. And like St John Bosco, let us bring the young to Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, God loves the whole world so much that he gave us Jesus! Jesus was lifted up on the Cross so that we can live with him for ever.
Look at a cross today and say: thank you, Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, on this Saturday at the close of the Nativity season Jesus puts a lamp into our hands. Be dressed for action and have your lamps lit, he says, like servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding banquet, ready to open the door as soon as he knocks (Luke 12:35–36).

Then he says something astonishing. Blessed are those servants whom the master finds alert: he will fasten his belt, have them sit down to eat, and come and serve them (Luke 12:37). Masters do not serve servants. This Master does. We have just seen him lying in a manger; we will see him kneeling to wash feet. The one we wait for is the one who serves.

How do we stay awake? St Paul says we have received not the spirit of the world but the Spirit that is from God, so that we may understand the gifts God gives us (1 Corinthians 2:12). The Spirit teaches us to discern: to recognise the Lord's knock in a word of Scripture, in a poor person at the gate, in the quiet voice of conscience.

A new year has just begun. We do not know at what hour the Lord will come, to the world or to each of us. You also must be ready, Jesus says (Luke 12:40). Let us keep our lamps lit with prayer and good works, so that whenever he knocks, we may open at once. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about servants who stayed awake at night with their lamps lit, waiting for their master. When he came, he served them dinner! Let us keep the lamp of our love for Jesus burning every day by praying and being kind.

homily: Dear friends, as Denha draws near the Church asks: who is this Child? Jesus answers in the Gospel: the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise (John 5:19).

This is the language of perfect unity. Jesus gives life as the Father gives life. He is entrusted with judgement. And all must honour the Son just as they honour the Father (John 5:23). The Child in the manger is worthy of the same worship as the Father.
St John tells us what this means for us. Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God (1 John 5:1). Faith is not only an opinion; it is a new birth.

And this new birth is powerful: whatever is born of God conquers the world. This is the victory that conquers the world, our faith (1 John 5:4). Fears, temptations and the pressures of the world do not have the last word over a child of God.
As Denha approaches, let us renew our faith in Jesus, the Son of the Father, and live this week as children who have already won. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus always does what his Father does, because they love each other. Watch the good things your parents do, and do the same!

homily: Dear friends, tonight is the eve of Denha. St Paul gives Titus a rule for the baptised: those who have come to believe in God must be careful to devote themselves to good works; these things are excellent and profitable to everyone (Titus 3:8). The faith we received in Baptism is meant to be seen in our hands.

Paul also warns against what drains a community's strength: stupid controversies, genealogies, dissensions and quarrels, which are unprofitable and worthless (Titus 3:9). How many families and parishes lose years in such arguments, while the poor wait at the door.

In the Gospel someone asks Jesus: Lord, will only a few be saved? Jesus gives no number. He says: strive to enter through the narrow door (Luke 13:23–24). It is not enough to say, we ate and drank with you. The Lord looks for a life he can recognise. And yet he promises that people will come from east and west, from north and south, and will eat in the kingdom of God (Luke 13:29).

Tomorrow Jesus goes down into the Jordan, and the door of heaven opens. Our ancestors kept this night with lamps on plantain stems, crying El Paiya, God is light, and with a bath that recalled the Jordan. Let us light a lamp in our hearts tonight, put aside one quarrel and do one good work, so that we may enter by the door he opens. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight is the eve of Denha! In many homes people light lamps and say: God is light! Light a lamp with your family, and do one good thing for someone before you go to sleep.

homily: Dear friends, on the day after Denha St Paul speaks of a wisdom that is not of this age. God's wisdom, secret and hidden, was decreed before the ages for our glory (1 Corinthians 2:7). The rulers of this age did not understand it; if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

This wisdom cannot be reached by cleverness. What no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor the human heart conceived, God has prepared for those who love him, and he has revealed it to us through the Spirit (1 Corinthians 2:9–10).

In the Gospel we see that wisdom with a human face. At the gate of Nain a widow follows the body of her only son. Nobody asks Jesus for help. He sees her, has compassion for her, and says: do not weep. He touches the bier and says: young man, I say to you, rise! And he gives him back to his mother (Luke 7:13–15).

The people cry out: a great prophet has risen among us; God has looked favourably on his people (Luke 7:16). This is the manifestation of Denha: God's wisdom is a compassion that stops at our funerals and gives life. Let us ask for it, and let us stop for those who weep. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus saw a mother crying because her son had died. He felt sorry for her and brought her son back to life! Jesus cares when we are sad. Let us care for sad people too.

homily: Dear friends, on the Fridays of Denha the Church remembers the witnesses of Christ. Today we honour John the Baptist, who saw the heavens open at the Jordan. Long before, Isaiah had heard a voice crying: in the wilderness prepare the way of the Lord (Isaiah 40:3). John was that voice.

In Antioch St Paul tells the story of Israel, from Egypt to King David, and then says: before the coming of Jesus, John proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people. And John said: I am not he; one is coming after me, and I am not worthy to untie his sandals (Acts 13:24–25). The greatness of John is that he points away from himself.

John told Herod: it is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife (Mark 6:18). Herod knew that John was a righteous and holy man, and even liked to listen to him. But at his birthday banquet, to keep a rash oath and to save face before his guests, he had John beheaded in prison. Truth spoken with love can be costly.

Where is Herod's power now? The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever (Isaiah 40:8). St Paul, writing as a prisoner for Christ, tells us that we are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone (Ephesians 2:20). John's witness, sealed in blood, is part of that foundation.
Let us ask for John's humility, to point always to Christ, and for his courage, to speak the truth with love. And let us pray for Christians who today are imprisoned or killed for their faith. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was very brave. He told the king the truth even when it was dangerous. Let us always tell the truth, kindly and bravely.

homily: Dear friends, in the season of Denha we keep asking: who is this Jesus revealed at the Jordan? In today's Gospel some in the Temple pick up stones to throw at him. Jesus asks: I have shown you many good works from the Father; for which of these are you going to stone me? (John 10:32).

They answer: not for a good work, but because you, though only a human being, are making yourself God (John 10:33). They understood his claim correctly; they refused to believe it. Jesus does not soften it. He is the one whom the Father has sanctified and sent into the world. Believe the works, he says, so that you may know that the Father is in me and I am in the Father (John 10:36–38).

St Paul looks at the same mystery. Gentiles who were not searching for righteousness received it through faith, while many who tried to earn it by works stumbled over the stumbling stone (Romans 9:30–32). Christ can be a stone we trip over, if we want to save ourselves by our own strength. Or he can be our foundation, for whoever believes in him will not be put to shame (Romans 9:33).
At the Jordan the Father said: this is my Son. Let us receive him by faith, look at his works in our lives and in the Church, and build everything on him. Amen.
kids: Children, some people did not believe that Jesus was God's Son. Jesus said: look at the good things I do! Let us thank Jesus for the good things he does for us, and do good things in his name.

homily: Dear friends, the Corinthians were a lively, gifted community, yet Paul has to write to them: when you come together as a church, I hear that there are divisions among you (1 Corinthians 11:18). At the Lord's supper the better-off ate their own meal while the poor went hungry.
Paul asks: do you show contempt for the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? (1 Corinthians 11:22). The meal of unity had become a sign of division.

In the Gospel Jesus prays for us, who believe through the apostles' word: that they may all be one, as you, Father, are in me and I am in you, so that the world may believe that you have sent me (John 17:21). Our unity is meant to be a window through which the world sees God.
In a week the Church begins the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity. Let us start at home: one phone call, one greeting, one apology before we next come to the altar. Amen.
kids: Children, before Jesus died, he prayed for you! He asked his Father that we would all be one big family. So be kind to everyone, even the child nobody plays with.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul says that the Church is like a body: one body, many members. In the one Spirit we were all baptized into one body (1 Corinthians 12:13). The foot cannot say: I do not belong, because I am not a hand.

Some of us think we are too important; others think we are not important at all. Both forget that God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose (1 Corinthians 12:18). You are needed in the Body of Christ.

Jesus gives the same lesson with a vine: I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing (John 15:5). The secret of a fruitful life is not effort alone but staying joined to him.
Sometimes the Father prunes us. It hurts, but he does it so that we may bear more fruit. Let us abide in his love through his word, through our prayer and through the Holy Qurbana. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says he is a vine and you are a little branch. Stay close to Jesus every day with a prayer, and you will grow lovely fruit: kindness, joy and peace!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul asks us to remember: once we were far off, strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world (Ephesians 2:12). According to our tradition, our ancestors in Kerala received the Gospel from the apostle Thomas. Christ came looking for us.

But now, says Paul, you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:13–14). In Christ no one is a foreigner. We are citizens with the saints and members of the household of God (Ephesians 2:19).
Who cares for this household? The risen Jesus asks Peter three times: do you love me? And each time he adds: feed my sheep (John 21:15–17). Before he gives Peter a task, he asks for his love.
Each of us has sheep to feed: our children, our students, the sick, the new family in the parish. Let us serve them out of love for Christ, and break down the walls that still divide us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked Peter: do you love me? Then take care of my sheep. You can take care of Jesus' sheep too: be a friend to the new child in your class!

homily: Dear friends, the disciples are crossing the lake at evening when a great windstorm arises and the waves begin to fill the boat. Jesus is asleep on a cushion. They wake him: Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing? (Mark 4:38).

Jesus rises and says to the sea: Peace! Be still! And there is a dead calm. Then he asks them: why are you afraid? Have you still no faith? (Mark 4:39–40). The disciples ask the question of Denha: who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

Years later Peter, who was in that boat, writes: cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you (1 Peter 5:7). And he warns: the devil prowls around like a roaring lion; resist him, steadfast in your faith (1 Peter 5:8–9).

Today we honour St Devasahayam. After his Baptism he would not deny Christ. For nearly three years he was kept in chains, and at Aralvaimozhy in 1752 he gave his life. The storm did not stop for him, but Christ was in his boat.
Let us hand our worries to the Lord who cares for us, and ask St Devasahayam to make us steadfast in faith. Amen.
kids: Children, once there was a big storm and the disciples were scared, but Jesus said: Peace! Be still! And the sea became calm. When you are scared, say: Jesus, you are in my boat. I trust you!

homily: Dear friends, on the Fridays of Denha the Church honours the great witnesses of Christ. Today: Peter and Paul, the pillars of the Church.

At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asks: but who do you say that I am? Simon Peter answers: you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God (Matthew 16:15–16). Jesus says that this did not come from flesh and blood but from his Father in heaven. And he adds: you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church (Matthew 16:18).

Peter carries that faith into the world. In Joppa he kneels beside the body of Tabitha, a woman full of good works, and says: Tabitha, get up. And she opens her eyes (Acts 9:40). Like Elisha long before him, but in the name of the risen Jesus, Peter brings life.

Paul tells us what it cost him: beatings, a stoning, shipwrecks, hunger, cold, and the daily anxiety for all the churches. And he says: if I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness (2 Corinthians 11:30).

Both gave their lives in Rome. Let us pray today for the Pope, Peter's successor, and for our bishops. And let us answer Jesus' question from our hearts: you are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked Peter: who do you say that I am? Peter said: you are the Son of God! And Jesus called him a rock. Tell Jesus today: you are the Son of God, and I love you!

homily: Dear friends, in the synagogue at Capernaum the people were astounded: Jesus taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes (Mark 1:22). His word does not only explain; it acts.

A man with an unclean spirit cries out: I know who you are, the Holy One of God. Jesus says: be silent, and come out of him! And the man is freed (Mark 1:24–25). Evil recognises its Master. The people ask: what is this? A new teaching, with authority!

St Paul tells us how this word reaches us: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved. But how can they call on one of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone to proclaim him? So faith comes from what is heard (Romans 10:13–14, 17).

Our faith came to us because someone was sent: an apostle, a missionary, a grandmother, a catechist. Now we are the ones sent. Let us believe with the heart, confess with the mouth, and let our feet carry the good news. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus' words are so strong that even bad spirits obey him! And somebody once told you about Jesus. This week you can tell a friend: Jesus loves you!

homily: Dear friends, today we begin the Three Days' Fast, the fast of the Ninevites. Our Church of the East first kept it in a time of plague, when the people fasted and begged God for mercy. The first reading gives us the words for that prayer.

A people back from exile looks at its ruins and cries: O that you would tear open the heavens and come down! They confess: all our righteous deeds are like a filthy cloth; we all fade like a leaf. Then comes the turn: yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter (Isaiah 64:8). A broken pot can be remade if it stays in the potter's hands.

Habakkuk teaches us to rejoice in God even when the fig tree does not blossom and the fields yield no food. And Paul asks that prayers be made for everyone, for kings and all in authority, because God desires everyone to be saved (1 Timothy 2:4). A rogation is the whole Church praying for the whole world.

But Jesus tells a hard parable. A servant is forgiven a debt he could never pay, then throttles a fellow servant over a small sum. The master asks: should you not have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you? (Matthew 18:33). If we ask God not to remember our sins, we cannot keep a list of the sins of others.
Today the Church Unity Octave also begins. Let our fast begin with forgiveness: in our families, in our parishes, and among divided Christians. Amen.
kids: Children, a king forgave a man a huge debt, but the man would not forgive his friend a tiny one. Jesus wants us to forgive like God forgives us. Is there someone you need to say sorry to, or forgive, today?

homily: Dear friends, on this second day of the fast, the readings ask: what kind of fast pleases God? At Mizpah Samuel tells Israel: if you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, put away the foreign gods (1 Samuel 7:3). The people pour out water before the LORD, fast and confess: we have sinned against the LORD. Samuel prays for them, and the LORD answers.

Isaiah answers those who complain that God does not hear: the LORD's hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. Rather, your iniquities have been barriers between you and your God (Isaiah 59:1–2). Fasting is the work of taking down those barriers, stone by stone.

Then Jesus tells of two men at prayer. The Pharisee fasts twice a week and gives a tenth of all his income. But his prayer is about himself, and he despises the tax collector. The tax collector stands far off, beats his breast and says: God, be merciful to me, a sinner (Luke 18:13). Jesus says this man went home justified.

Notice: the Pharisee fasted. Fasting is not the problem. Pride is the problem. Paul tells us not to think of ourselves more highly than we ought, because we, who are many, are one body in Christ (Romans 12:3, 5). A fast that makes us look down on others has missed its goal.
In this Unity Octave, let us pray the tax collector's prayer for ourselves and for all Christians. God, be merciful to us, sinners, and make us one. Amen.
kids: Children, one man said to God: I am so good! Another man said: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. Jesus liked the second prayer. Let us pray it today: Jesus, have mercy on me.

homily: Dear friends, on the last day of our fast we read the story that gave it its name. Jonah walks into Nineveh and cries: forty days more, and Nineveh shall be overthrown! And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth (Jonah 3:5).

The king leaves his throne and sits in ashes. He says: who knows? God may relent. And when God saw how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity, and he did not do it (Jonah 3:10). Joel shows the same: blow the trumpet, sanctify a fast, gather even the infants, let the priests weep at the altar: spare your people, O LORD. And the LORD had pity on his people (Joel 2:15–18).

Paul says God gathers objects of mercy from every nation: those who were not my people I will call my people (Romans 9:25). Nineveh was a pagan city, and God had pity on it. No one is outside his mercy.

Jesus warns us not to spoil the fast at the end. Beware of practicing your piety before others in order to be seen by them. When you give alms, let your left hand not know what your right hand is doing, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you (Matthew 6:1–4). Let us give quietly what we have saved by fasting.

Today we honour St Sebastian and pray for our bishops who bear his name. He served Christ quietly among the soldiers, and when the time came he confessed him openly, without fear. Let us end this fast the same way: mercy in secret, faith without fear. Amen.
kids: Children, the whole city of Nineveh said sorry to God, even the king and the little children, and God forgave them! Today, do one kind thing for someone without telling anybody. Only God will know.

homily: Dear friends, the Three Days' Fast is over, and today the Church celebrates God's joy. Through Ezekiel God swears: as I live, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live (Ezekiel 33:11).

Micah sings: who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity? He delights in showing clemency. You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea (Micah 7:18–19). What we brought to God in these three days, he has thrown into the sea.

In the Gospel Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one, and of a woman who searches her whole house for one coin. When they find them they say: rejoice with me. Just so, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:6–7).
John the Elder writes: I have no greater joy than this, to hear that my children are walking in the truth (3 John 4). Let the fruit of our fast be joy, and let us become seekers of the lost. Amen.
kids: Children, a shepherd found his lost sheep and was so happy! God is that happy when we come back to him. Thank God for these three days of fasting.

homily: Dear friends, on the third Friday of Denha we honour the four Evangelists. The first reading takes us to Mount Carmel. Elijah rebuilds the broken altar of the LORD with twelve stones, pours water on the offering three times, and prays: answer me, O LORD, so that this people may know that you are God. The fire falls, and the people cry: the LORD indeed is God (1 Kings 18:39).

Denha means manifestation: God showing himself. In Acts he shows himself again: many signs and wonders are done through the apostles, and people lay the sick in the streets hoping Peter's shadow will fall on them (Acts 5:12–15).

In the Gospel Jesus calls the Twelve by name and sends them: as you go, proclaim the good news, the kingdom of heaven has come near. You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:7–8). Matthew and John were among them. Mark and Luke learned from Peter and Paul. What the apostles preached, the Evangelists wrote, so that the good news could reach us.

It was not easy. Paul says: we are fools for the sake of Christ, hungry, poorly clothed, homeless. But he also says: in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel (1 Corinthians 4:15). Each time we open a Gospel, these fathers in faith speak to us. Let us read one Gospel this month, and pass on freely what we have freely received. Amen.
kids: Children, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John wrote down the story of Jesus for us! Jesus said: you received for free, so give for free. Share something with a friend today, and read a little of the Gospel every day.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes from prison to the Philippians: live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ, standing firm in one spirit, striving side by side with one mind for the faith of the gospel (Philippians 1:27). In this Unity Octave, that is God's word to all Christians.
He even says that suffering for Christ is a privilege, a gift of grace (Philippians 1:29). Christians who suffer together for the Gospel discover how much unites them.

In the Gospel a Canaanite woman cries: have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David. Jesus does not answer. The disciples want her sent away. She kneels and says only: Lord, help me (Matthew 15:25). And when Jesus speaks of the children's food, she answers: yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.

Jesus says: woman, great is your faith! (Matthew 15:28). She is a foreigner, yet she shows the disciples what faith is: humble, persistent, sure that a crumb from Christ is enough. When God seems silent, let us not give up. Let us say with her: Lord, help me. Amen.
kids: Children, a mother kept asking Jesus to help her sick daughter, even when it seemed he said no. Jesus said: great is your faith! Let us never stop praying. Say with her today: Lord, help me!

homily: Dear friends, today two great calls are set side by side. Moses, a shepherd in the desert, sees a bush burning and not consumed, and hears: Moses, Moses! God reveals his name: I AM WHO I AM (Exodus 3:14).

Saul, on the road to Damascus, is thrown down by a light from heaven and hears: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? He asks: who are you, Lord? The answer: I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting (Acts 9:4–5). The God of the burning bush now has a human face, and he suffers in his Church.
Blind, Saul is led into Damascus. Ananias lays hands on him; something like scales fall from his eyes; he is baptized, and immediately proclaims Jesus as the Son of God.
Years later Paul writes: last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me. And: by the grace of God I am what I am (1 Corinthians 15:8, 10).

The Gospel explains this grace. Workers hired at five o'clock receive the same wage as those hired at dawn. The owner says: are you envious because I am generous? (Matthew 20:15). Paul came late and received the full wage of grace.
None of us earns salvation; all of us receive it. Let us give thanks for grace, rejoice in others' blessings, and pray today that all Christians may be one. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul started by hurting Christians, but Jesus changed him into his best messenger. God's love is for everyone, even people who come late!
Let us be happy when others get good things, because God is generous.

opts.a: Ananias, the disciple who was afraid
intro: Every conversion story has two heroes: the one who is converted, and the one who dares to welcome him. Today we look at Ananias.

points.apply: Tell God honestly what you fear about someone.

points.h: Go, for he is my chosen instrument
points.apply: Pray for someone you have written off.
Welcome a newcomer or a returning Catholic as brother or sister.

concl: Without Ananias there might have been no Paul.
God still needs disciples brave enough to say brother.
opts.resolve: This week I will reach out to one person I have been afraid of or have given up on.
homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate the conversion of Paul. But there is another hero in the story, a quiet disciple in Damascus named Ananias.

The Lord said to him: get up and go to the street called Straight, and look for a man of Tarsus named Saul. Ananias answered honestly: Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to your saints (Acts 9:11, 13). He was afraid, and he had good reason to be.

But the Lord said: go, for he is an instrument whom I have chosen to bring my name before Gentiles and kings (Acts 9:15). God sees what we cannot see. The man everyone feared was the man God had chosen.
So Ananias went, laid his hands on Saul and said: Brother Saul (Acts 9:17). His first word was brother. Something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he was baptised.

Who is the Saul in my life? The person I fear, avoid, or have given up on? Perhaps God is sending me, as he sent Ananias, to say: brother, sister. And let us bring that person to the Holy Qurbana in our prayer today. Amen.

intro: Saul did not change his zeal, his intelligence or his energy. He changed his centre. Conversion is not becoming someone else but becoming who God meant.

points.apply: Name one thing you are proud of and offer it to Christ.
Make a good confession this week.

sub: Faith in the Son of God who loved me.
points.apply: Pray each morning: Lord, live in me today.

concl: Conversion keeps our gifts but changes our centre.
Paul's zeal became love for Christ and for all peoples.
opts.resolve: Each morning this week I will pray Galatians 2:20: it is Christ who lives in me.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, what changed when Saul became Paul? Not his intelligence: he remained a brilliant scholar. Not his energy: he remained tireless. Not his zeal: he remained on fire. What changed was the centre of his life.

He writes: whatever gains I had, these I have come to regard as loss because of Christ (Philippians 3:7). His birth, his learning, his religious record, all the things he had been proud of, he now laid at the feet of Christ.

He discovered that if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new (2 Corinthians 5:17). This is what happens in every good confession: the old passes, the new begins.

And he could finally say: it is no longer I who live, but it is Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me (Galatians 2:20).

God does not want to destroy our gifts but to set them on the right centre. Let us offer him our pride, make a good confession, and pray each day: Lord, live in me. And receive him in the Holy Qurbana as Paul's whole life. Amen.
Dear friends, Hebrews tells us that God's promised rest is still open, and that God sets a day for us: today. Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 4:7).

At Nazareth the people first admire Jesus' gracious words, then ask: is not this Joseph's son? (Luke 4:22). They think they know him too well to listen. Jesus says: no prophet is accepted in the prophet's hometown (Luke 4:24), and reminds them that God's mercy reached a widow of Sidon and a Syrian general.

Today is Republic Day. Our Constitution promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all. Christians serve this nation by listening to God today, by rejecting contempt, and by welcoming every neighbour of every faith.

We also honour Sts Timothy and Titus, whom Paul told to fight the good fight of the faith (1 Timothy 6:12). Let us thank God for India, pray for those who govern, and keep our hearts soft to his voice. Amen.
kids: Children, the people of Nazareth did not listen to Jesus because they thought he was just Joseph's son. Let us listen to Jesus today, and pray for our country India!

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes to the Galatians in alarm: I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting the one who called you in the grace of Christ (Galatians 1:6). There is no other gospel, because there is no other Christ.
Then he examines his own heart: if I were still pleasing people, I would not be a servant of Christ (Galatians 1:10). The temptation to please people is strong for every disciple.
In the Gospel Jesus says the shepherd calls his own sheep by name and leads them out, and the sheep follow him because they know his voice (John 10:3–4). They will not follow a stranger.
We learn the Shepherd's voice by listening every day, in Scripture, in the Holy Qurbana and in the teaching of the Church. Then no stranger's voice will lead us away. Amen.
kids: Children, a good shepherd knows the name of every sheep! Jesus knows your name. Let us listen to him every day so that we know his voice.

homily: Dear friends, Paul says: the love of Christ urges us on, because we are convinced that one has died for all (2 Corinthians 5:14). Christ's love is like a current that carries us toward others.

In the Gospel John points to Jesus: look, here is the Lamb of God! Two disciples follow. Jesus turns and asks: what are you looking for? (John 1:38). They ask where he is staying, and he says: come and see. They remain with him that day.
Then Andrew finds his brother Simon and says: we have found the Messiah (John 1:41). He brings him to Jesus, who gives him a new name. This is how Christ is made known: one person tells another.

St Thomas Aquinas, whom we honour today, gave his great mind to Christ. The early accounts tell that when the Lord asked him what reward he wanted, he answered: nothing but you, Lord. May we too seek nothing but Christ, and bring others to him. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked two friends: what are you looking for? Then he said: come and see! Who can you invite to come and see Jesus?

homily: Dear friends, Naboth refuses to sell his family vineyard to the king: the LORD forbid that I should give you my ancestral inheritance (1 Kings 21:3). He is falsely accused and stoned. Jesus laments over Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those sent to it, which he longed to gather as a hen gathers her brood (Matthew 23:37).

Stephen is the next in that line. But filled with the Holy Spirit he looks up and says: I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God (Acts 7:56). He dies praying: Lord, do not hold this sin against them.

Saul held the coats. Years later, as Paul, he writes: we are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; always carrying in the body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our bodies (2 Corinthians 4:8, 10).
So let us look not at what can be seen but at what cannot be seen. The stones are real, but the glory is greater. Let us carry Christ in our troubles and forgive as Stephen forgave. Amen.
kids: Children, St Stephen looked up and saw Jesus in heaven, even when people hurt him. He forgave them! When someone hurts us, let us look to Jesus and pray for them.

homily: Dear friends, John writes so that you may know that you have eternal life (1 John 5:13). We can pray with boldness, because if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.

John even tells us what to pray for: a brother or sister who sins. He distinguishes mortal sin from sin that is not mortal, as the Church still does, and promises that God will give life to the one for whom we pray. Instead of judging, we intercede.
In the Gospel Jesus tells those who boast of Abraham: if you were Abraham's children, you would be doing what Abraham did (John 8:39). And: whoever is from God hears the words of God (John 8:47).
Tomorrow is the Lord's Day. Today let us keep ourselves from idols and from lies, pray for one another, and prepare our hearts through confession. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says God's children listen to God and tell the truth. Today, let us pray for someone who has done wrong, and say sorry for our own mistakes.

intro: Theme: “You are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”
The Holy Name at the start of the year: called by name, saved, exalted.

sub: A new name, a new mission.
q: But now thus says the LORD, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
points.apply: Learn the meaning of your baptismal name and thank God for it.

sub: Call on him in every need.
q: Then everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved;
She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
points.apply: Pray the Jesus Prayer each morning this year.

q: To me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.
Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
points.apply: Never use the Lord's name carelessly; bow your head when you hear it.

concl: The year begins with the Name that saves.
With Mary, Mother of God, let us carry this Name into every day.
2027-01-01.resolve: Consecrate the new year to Jesus tonight as a family.

intro: Theme: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
God hears, sends and anoints: from the burning bush to Nazareth.

sub: The bush burns but is not consumed.
God sees the misery of his people.
q: Then the LORD said, “I have observed the misery of my people who are in Egypt; I have heard their cry on account of their taskmasters. Indeed, I know their sufferings,

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free,
points.apply: Find one person in need this week and help them.

points.h: Who am I? I will be with you
sub: God offers no flattery, only his presence.
Every mission rests on this promise.
q: He said, “I will be with you; and this shall be the sign for you that it is I who sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall worship God on this mountain.”
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Take up one task you have been avoiding, trusting God's presence.

q: I will give you the treasures of darkness and riches hidden in secret places, so that you may know that it is I, the LORD, the God of Israel, who call you by your name.
Then he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
points.apply: Read Luke 4:16–22 slowly before Denha.

q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.

But as for you, continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it, and how from childhood you have known the sacred writings that are able to instruct you for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Pray and read Scripture with your children this week.

concl: The God of the burning bush has come down in Jesus, the Anointed.
St Chavara shows the fruit: faith handed on, the poor raised up.
2027-01-03.resolve: Prepare for Denha on Wednesday with a family reading of the Gospel and a good confession.

intro: Theme: “This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.”
Denha: the dawn of the Trinity's revelation and of our Baptism.

sub: Balaam sees a star from afar.
The dawn rises at the Jordan.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silent adoration today.

sub: The Spirit of wisdom and might.
q: The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
And when Jesus had been baptized, just as he came up from the water, suddenly the heavens were opened to him and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

q: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.
And a voice from heaven said, “This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.”
points.apply: Make the Sign of the Cross slowly and with faith each time you pray.

q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
he saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Find your baptismal date and celebrate it.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opened, and it has not closed.
We are baptised: let us live as the Father's beloved.
2027-01-06.resolve: Keep holy water at home and bless your family each night.

intro: Theme: “Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.”
The God who travelled with Israel has pitched his tent among us in Jesus.

sub: The ark seeks a resting place for them.
q: So they set out from the mount of the LORD three days' journey with the ark of the covenant of the LORD going before them three days' journey, to seek out a resting place for them,
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Each morning pray: Arise, O Lord, go before me today.

sub: No one has ever seen God.
The Son has made him known.
q: Truly, you are a God who hides himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.
No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, who has made him known.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

q: Not so with my servant Moses; he is entrusted with all my house.
Christ, however, was faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for your parish, God's house where you live.

q: The LORD passed before him, and proclaimed, “The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,
From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. The law indeed was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Each night write down one grace you received that day.

concl: The God who went before Israel now dwells among us in Christ.
From his fullness we receive grace upon grace.
2027-01-10.resolve: Read John 1:1–18 slowly this week and thank God for one grace each day.

intro: Theme: “I will carry and will save.”
Who carries whom? Moses cannot, idols cannot; God carries, and the Lamb takes away the sin of the world.

sub: The Spirit shared with the elders.
q: I am not able to carry all this people alone, for they are too heavy for me.
Bear one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
points.apply: Carry part of someone's burden this week.

points.h: I will carry and will save
sub: Bel and Nebo on weary animals.
God carries from the womb to gray hair.
q: even to your old age I am he, even when you turn gray I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save.
Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Name one idol you carry and put it down during the fast.

q: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: Make a good confession during the Three Days' Fast.

q: O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
So then, a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God; for those who enter God’s rest also cease from their labors as God did from his.
points.apply: Keep Sunday as a day of rest with God and family.

concl: Idols are carried; the true God carries us.
The Lamb takes away our sin and leads us into his rest.
2027-01-17.resolve: Keep the Three Days' Fast faithfully this week, handing your burdens to the Lamb of God.

intro: Theme: “Do whatever he tells you.”
Christ reveals his glory: the unlimited power of God, the God who carries, the good wine, the eternal priest.

q: The LORD said to Moses, “Is the LORD's power limited? Now you shall see whether my word will come true for you or not.”
Jesus answered, “Do you believe because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”
points.apply: Bring one impossible situation to God in prayer today.

q: remember the former things of old; for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is no one like me,
Nathanael replied, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
points.apply: Name one idol you carry, and set it down.

q: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph; what he says to you, do.”
His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
points.apply: Obey one clear word of the Gospel this week.

points.h: The good wine kept until now
q: The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: Receive the Holy Qurbana this Sunday as the good wine of the Bridegroom.

concl: At Cana the God of unlimited power reveals his glory in a small village.
Tell him what has run out, and do whatever he tells you.
2027-01-24.resolve: Each evening this week, tell Jesus one need of your family.

intro: Theme: “For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.”
Christ revealed as the Prophet like Moses, the Son lifted up, and the Light of the world.

q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
While he was still speaking, suddenly a bright cloud overshadowed them, and from the cloud a voice said, “This is my Son, the Beloved; with him I am well pleased; listen to him!”
points.apply: Put away every horoscope and lucky charm; listen to Christ.

points.h: The God who teaches and leads
q: Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your own good, who leads you in the way you should go.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
points.apply: Ask God each morning this week to lead you in the way you should go.

q: So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon a pole; and whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
points.apply: Spend five minutes daily before a crucifix.

q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
But those who do what is true come to the light, so that it may be clearly seen that their deeds have been done in God.”
points.apply: Bring one hidden fault into the light of confession.

concl: God has spoken in his Son and lifted him up for our salvation.
Leave the darkness, look at the Cross, and come to the light.
2027-01-31.resolve: Go to confession this week and place a crucifix where your family will see it.

intro: Theme: “You also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an unexpected hour.”
The Spirit gives discernment; the servant keeps the lamp lit.

sub: Only our own spirit knows our heart.
q: The human spirit is the lamp of the LORD, searching every inmost part.
Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that is from God, so that we may understand the gifts bestowed on us by God.
points.apply: Begin each day this week with the prayer: Come, Holy Spirit.

sub: The unspiritual call God's gifts foolish.
Discernment is a gift to ask for.
q: Give your servant therefore an understanding mind to govern your people, able to discern between good and evil;
Those who are spiritual discern all things, and they are themselves subject to no one else's scrutiny.
points.apply: Bring one decision of this new year to prayer before you make it.

points.h: Lamps lit for the Master who serves
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds alert when he comes; truly I tell you, he will fasten his belt and have them sit down to eat, and he will come and serve them.
points.apply: Examine your conscience briefly every night this week.

concl: The Spirit opens our eyes; the lamp keeps them open.
The one we wait for comes to serve us.
2027-01-02.resolve: Keep a short nightly examination of conscience all through January.

intro: Theme: “This is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.”
The Son one with the Father; believers born of God.

sub: Love for the Father includes his children.
q: Is not he your father, who created you, who made you and established you?
Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the parent loves the child.
points.apply: Thank God today for your Baptism.

points.h: The Son does the Father's works
sub: Honour the Son as the Father.
q: then I was beside him, like a master worker; and I was daily his delight, rejoicing before him always,
Jesus said to them, “Very truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.
points.apply: Pray the Glory Be with full attention each time today.

q: With the LORD on my side I do not fear. What can mortals do to me?
for whatever is born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.
points.apply: Make an act of faith whenever fear rises.

concl: The Child is the eternal Son, worthy of all honour.
Born of God, we share his victory.
2027-01-04.resolve: Prepare for Denha by renewing your baptismal promises.

intro: Theme: “Strive to enter through the narrow door.”
Good works, not quarrels; the narrow door opened at the Jordan.

q: learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.

The saying is sure. I desire that you insist on these things, so that those who have come to believe in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works; these things are excellent and profitable to everyone.
points.apply: Do one concrete good work for a neighbour this week.

sub: Unity is a work of faith.
q: The beginning of strife is like letting out water; so stop before the quarrel breaks out.
But avoid stupid controversies, genealogies, dissensions, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and worthless.
points.apply: Let go of one argument you keep returning to.

sub: Will only a few be saved?
From east and west to the feast.
q: This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it.
Strive to enter through the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
points.apply: Light a lamp tonight and pray for all who seek the door of faith.

concl: Tomorrow Christ goes down into the Jordan and the door of heaven opens.
Let us enter with lamps lit and hands full of good works.
2027-01-05.resolve: Keep the Denha eve with a lamp, family prayer and one good work.

intro: Theme: “A great prophet has risen among us!”
The hidden wisdom of God, revealed in compassion.

sub: Not the wisdom of this age.
q: For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding;
But we speak God's wisdom, secret and hidden, which God decreed before the ages for our glory.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit for wisdom each time you open the Scriptures.

sub: Prepared for those who love him.
q: From ages past no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides you, who works for those who wait for him.
But, as it is written, “What no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor the human heart conceived, what God has prepared for those who love him”
points.apply: Make an act of love for God each morning this week.

sub: He gives him to his mother.
q: Elijah took the child, brought him down from the upper chamber into the house, and gave him to his mother; then Elijah said, “See, your son is alive.”
When the Lord saw her, he had compassion for her and said to her, “Do not weep.”
points.apply: Visit or call someone who is grieving.

concl: God's wisdom is not cold knowledge but compassion that gives life.
In Denha, God has looked favourably on his people.
2027-01-07.resolve: Stop this week for someone in sorrow.

intro: Theme: “The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.”
John the Baptist: the voice, the witness, the martyr.

sub: All people shall see God's glory.
q: A voice cries out: In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
before his coming John had already proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
points.apply: Make one thing straight in your life this week: a confession, an apology, a debt repaid.

q: I will also speak of your decrees before kings, and shall not be put to shame.
For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.”
points.apply: Speak one hard truth this week, gently and with love.

points.h: Built on the apostles and prophets
q: The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone.

So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for the persecuted Church.

concl: Herod's power withered; John's witness still speaks.
Truth with love, built on Christ the cornerstone.
